papers.title: 3D bioprinting of flap-tissue with heterogenous cells and flexible perfusable vessels.
papers.abstract: Despite advancements in bio-manufacturing, the fabrication of large-scale vascularized tissue with heterogeneous cells remains a daunting challenge. To address this challenge, the reverse engineered structured tissue (REST) three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting method was proposed. This strategy enables the seeding and subsequent assembly of multiple tissue-specific constituent cells onto a robust, flexible, 3D biomimetic vascular scaffold with long-term perfusion capability. The material choices for the vessel network and seeding cells could be decoupled, and separate co-culture of multiple seeding cells in a customized bioreactor could be realized. The cellular layers could be reassembled into an engineered tissue by manually folding the robust vessels. Centimeter-scale vascularized skin-flap-like tissues that comprise epidermal, dermal, and adipose layers were engineered with an in vivo-like communicating vascular network using this strategy. The engineered tissue exhibits three-layered cellular heterogeneity (containing HaCaT cells, fibroblasts, and adipose-derived stem cells) and perfusable tubes (containing HUVECs and VSMCs). The complex tissue could be remolded through in vitro perfusion of vessel network and specific culture/differentiation medium supplied to tissue-specific cellular layers. After in vivo transplantation for three months, the tissue construct formed a viable complex tissue with a rich network of blood vessels. Our results demonstrate that "REST" bioprinting technology can be used to fabricate multicellular tissues, ranging from millimeter to centimeter scales with perfusable vessels, opening new avenues for functional artificial organ bioprinting.

papers.title: Atomic-scale ordering enables intrinsic bioactivity and rapid osseointegration in medium-entropy alloys.
papers.abstract: Conventional alloys achieve mechanical reliability and corrosion resistance at the expense of bioactivity, necessitating exogenous surface treatments that introduce long-term interfacial instability. In this study, we demonstrate that atomic-scale ordering, specifically the coexistence of chemical short-range order (CSRO) and ordered oxygen complexes (OOCs), can intrinsically integrate these otherwise contradictory requirements within a single metallic system. This strategy exploits the principle that atomic arrangements governing bulk mechanical behavior concurrently regulate surface physicochemical properties, thereby eliminating the need for extrinsic modification. A Ti-30Zr-14Nb-3O medium-entropy alloy (MEA) designed with CSRO-OOCs synergy exhibits bone-matched elastic modulus (∼42 GPa) and high yield strength (∼1040 MPa), overcoming the conventional strength-modulus trade-off. Importantly, this atomic configuration intrinsically generates nanoscale surface roughness (Ra ∼50.80 nm) and optimized surface energy distribution-features typically achieved only through artificial surface engineering. These ordering-regulated surface characteristics promote accelerated osteogenic differentiation in vitro without additional surface treatment. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal enhanced Ca2+ and PO4 3- adsorption on OOC-enabled surfaces, facilitating early calcium phosphate nucleation. In a rat cranial defect model, this intrinsic bioactivity translates into rapid, continuous bone formation along the implant surface, achieving a bone surface (BS) value of 70.63 ± 21.35 mm2 at 4 weeks, which was 3.5 times greater than that of the control group and significantly exceeds that of TC4. This work establishes atomic-scale ordering as a promising design framework for integrating mechanical compatibility with enhanced spontaneous osteoconductivity in metallic biomaterials.

papers.title: Bioengineered titanium implants functionalized with aptamer-valproic acid conjugates orchestrate macrophage programming and mesenchymal stem cell homing for improved osseointegration.
papers.abstract: Conventional titanium implants often exhibit limited bioactivity, failing to adequately modulate the immune response and promote endogenous regeneration, which leads to suboptimal osseointegration. To address this, we developed a multifunctional implant (NTP/Apt-VPA) by conjugating Apt19s-an mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-specific aptamer-with valproic acid (VPA), anchored onto a polydopamine-coated TiO2 nanotubular surface. The NTP/Apt-VPA implant demonstrated exceptional capabilities in scavenging reactive oxygen species, programming macrophages toward the regenerative M2 phenotype, and enhancing the recruitment and osteogenic differentiation of MSCs. Through comprehensive in vitro and in vivo assessments, as well as RNA sequencing analysis, we observed that the modified implant was associated with accelerated early inflammation resolution, enhanced stem cell homing, and activation of key osteogenic pathways, including PI3K/AKT and MAPK signaling. This study presents a bioengineering strategy that aims to synchronize immunomodulation with osteogenesis through an Apt19s-VPA conjugate, which may offer a promising platform for enhancing implant osseointegration.

papers.title: Integrated apoptotic extracellular vesicle-recruitment peptide coating reprograms the diabetic bone microenvironment and orchestrates enhanced implant osseointegration.
papers.abstract: Achieving stable prosthetic fixation remains a formidable challenge under diabetic conditions, primarily due to deficient osseointegration driven by impaired macrophage polarization and persistent inflammatory dysregulation within the bone microenvironment. To overcome these challenges, apoptotic extracellular vesicles (ApoEVs) harvested from osteogenically induced bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) were further modified with the stem cell-recruiting peptide EPLQLKM (E7). By leveraging mussel-inspired adhesive peptides and bio-orthogonal click conjugation, we achieved mild but stable immobilization of the modified ApoEVs onto titanium (Ti) surfaces. The ApoEV/E7-modified surface effectively inhibited the formation of M1 macrophages and the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, while promoting the formation of M2 macrophages and the expression of anti-inflammatory cytokines, thereby improving the inflammatory microenvironment at the diabetic bone-implant interface. Simultaneously, the modified surface stimulated angiogenesis under diabetes-induced inflammatory conditions and enhanced osteogenic activity. In vivo experiments demonstrated that implants with this modified surface enhanced bone tissue regeneration and bone structure restoration at the bone-implant interface in a diabetic inflammatory environment, effectively regulating inflammation at the bone-implant interface and promoting angiogenesis. Collectively, this study suggests that the 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine-ApoEV/E7 biomimetic coating effectively enhances interfacial osseointegration via immunomodulation and provides a promising strategy for the design of implant coatings aimed at enhancing osseointegration under diabetic conditions.

papers.title: Are there biomechanical differences in repair technique for lesser tuberosity osteotomy with stemless total shoulder arthroplasty?
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) has evolved as a treatment for advanced shoulder osteoarthrosis, with stemless implants gaining popularity due to reduced risks of stress shielding and complications associated with stemmed designs. However, the optimal technique for repairing the subscapularis with lesser tuberosity osteotomy (LTO) during TSA remains under investigation. This study evaluates the biomechanical performance of two repair techniques-bone tunneling and suture anchors-used for LTO in the context of stemless TSA. METHODS: Ten shoulders from 6 cadaveric specimens (3 males and 3 females; aged 58-93 years old) were prepared and allocated to bone tunneling or suture anchor repair groups. Cyclic loading tests were performed, followed by incremental load-to-failure protocols. Outcomes included repair gapping during cyclic loading, initial repair stiffness (derived as the average secant stiffness for 10 of the initial 3,000 cycles prior to fatigue), cycles to failure, displacement of repair, and load to failure. RESULTS: The mean age of the cadavers used in this study was 90.2 ± 14.7 years. Mean failure load were alike, and cycles to failure nearly identical, between groups (P = .86-1.00). No significant differences were observed between the two groups in repair gapping during cyclic loading (P = .42). However, a nonsignificant trend was observed for initial repair stiffness (P = .07), with the tunnel group showing greater stiffness (62.5 ± 13.9 N/mm) compared to the anchor group (46.0 ± 10.6 N/mm). A trend was also noted in displacement of repair (P = .099), with the tunnel group exhibiting greater displacement (41.4 ± 17.3 mm) than the anchor group (23.0 ± 13.1 mm). CONCLUSION: This study suggests that both techniques may yield comparable biomechanical outcomes in cadaveric models of LTO repair, which warrants further exploration. As a pilot project, this study lays the groundwork for future research that could expand upon these preliminary results and contribute to a deeper understanding of LTO repair techniques.

papers.title: Clinical Value of an Artificial-intelligence-based Metal Artifact Correction Algorithm on Pelvic Computed Tomography After Hip Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Objective: To investigate the performance of an artificial-intelligence–based metal artifact correction algorithm (AIMAC) on pelvic computed tomography (CT) after total hip arthroplasty. Methods: This retrospective study included data from 34 patients with a history of hip arthroplasty who underwent pelvic CT at our institution between September 2022 and December 2024. Raw data were reconstructed using three methods: routine reconstruction (Karl 3D, level 5), conventional metal artifact correction (MAC), and AIMAC. For subjective evaluation, two radiologists independently scored overall image quality using a five-point scale in a blinded manner, and inter-reader agreement was assessed using the Kappa statistic. For objective evaluation, regions of interest were drawn to calculate CT-number differences between the artifact-affected and reference slices (ΔCTmuscle and ΔCTfat), standard deviation (SDartifact and SDreference), the metal artifact index (MAI), and the contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR). Overall comparisons among the three reconstructions were performed using repeated-measures analysis of variance or the Friedman test, according to normality. Pairwise comparisons were conducted using the paired t-test or the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with Holm–Bonferroni adjustment for multiple comparisons (P*). Results: Inter-reader agreement for overall image quality was good (Kappa: 0.866, 0.816, and 0.794). Overall subjective scores differed significantly among the three methods, with AIMAC scoring higher than MAC, and MAC scoring higher than routine reconstruction. For objective metrics, the ΔCTmuscle, ΔCTfat, SDartifact, MAI, and CNR all had significant differences among the three methods, with AIMAC outperforming MAC and routine reconstruction. For SDreference, MAC was lower than routine reconstruction and AIMAC, whereas no significant difference was observed between routine reconstruction and AIMAC. Conclusion: For pelvic CT after hip arthroplasty, AIMAC more effectively reduced metal artifacts, improved CT-number stability, and enhanced overall image quality compared with routine reconstruction and conventional MAC.

papers.title: Application of Multimodal Reconstruction Scheme on Periprosthetic Vasculature Visualization and Metal Artifact Reduction in Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Objective: To explore the combination of spectral computed tomography (CT) monochromatic imaging with a metal artifact reduction (MAR) algorithm and deep learning reconstruction (DLR). We also aimed to evaluate the image quality improvements in computed tomography angiography (CTA) of the lower extremity arteries after total hip arthroplasty (THA) using the DLR algorithm. Methods: A total of 24 patients who underwent dual-energy CTA examination of the lower-extremity arteries after hip replacement were retrospectively enrolled. The original dual-energy CTA data were reconstructed using four schemes: group A (conventional mixed-energy images), group B (conventional image+MAR), group C (conventional mixed-energy image+DLR), and group D (single energy+MAR+DLR). The subjective scores (5-point scale) of the four groups of images were compared with the objective parameters CT value, noise (SD), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and artifact index (AI)) of the femoral artery and adjacent subcutaneous fat at the metal artifact level. Analysis of variance and the weighted Kappa test were used for statistical comparisons. Results: Except for SNR, the differences in the other objective indices among the four groups were significant. In group D, AI decreased with increasing kiolelectron volt (keV); however, vessel enhancement, SNR, and CNR decreased with increasing keV. The 60 keV images had the highest overall score (4.89±0.32), which achieved the best balance between vessel display and artifact suppression. When the energy level was >70 keV, the changes in the AI value and the vessel noise plateaued. Conclusion: The triple scheme of spectral CT monochromatic energy imaging (60 keV), MAR algorithm, and DLR technology can effectively suppress metal artifacts and improve the definition of vascular structures after THA, which has certain clinical application value.

papers.title: FORMULATION AND OPTIMIZATION OF PHARMACEUTICAL HYDROGELS: A COMPREHENSIVE OVERVIEW
papers.abstract: Pharmaceutical hydrogels have profoundly altered the landscape of contemporary medicine, transforming them from passive, simple materials to bio-responsive, dynamic therapeutic systems. This comprehensive review explores the fundamental characteristics, evolutionary history, and classification of hydrogels, highlighting their unique ability to resemble human tissue as a result of their exceptional water-retention capabilities. The essential formulation and synthesis strategies are discussed, and physical cross-linking techniques, such as freeze-thawing and ionic interactions, are compared to robust chemical methods, such as free radical polymerisation and “click” chemistry. The integration of secondary nanocarriers, such as liposomes, to prevent premature burst release is a comprehensive study that involves the optimisation of release kinetics, which is influenced by diffusion, swelling, and degradation. This is essential for the precise delivery of drugs. Furthermore, the review emphasises the significance of Quality by Design (QbD) principles in the meticulous engineering of these intricate matrices to guarantee clinical safety and pharmacological efficacy. Lastly, we underscore the critical role of stimuli-responsive “smart” hydrogels as biomimetic scaffolds in advanced tissue engineering, particularly for the restoration of the central nervous system and 3D bioprinting, as well as their innovative applications. In summary, this summary provides a fundamental framework for the ongoing clinical translation of hydrogel therapies of the next generation.

papers.title: Total hip arthroplasty improves global sagittal and coronal spinal imbalance and spinopelvic mobility
papers.abstract: Aims The impact of total hip arthroplasty (THA) on global spinal alignment is under-reported. This study prospectively evaluates the effect of THA on coronal and sagittal global spinal balance and spinopelvic kinematics using dynamic whole-body EOS radiographs. Methods We prospectively studied 163 patients (62 male, 101 female; mean age 68.4 years (SD 9.1)) undergoing primary unilateral THA for end-stage osteoarthritis. Full-body EOS images were acquired preoperatively and at a six-month follow-up in standing, relaxed-seated, and deep-seated postures. The primary outcome was change in sagittal vertical axis (SVA). Secondary outcomes included changes in pelvic tilt (PT), sacral slope (SS), proximal femoral angle (PFA), and coronal parameters (C7-central sacral vertical line (C7-CSVL), limb length discrepancy (LLD), and pelvic obliquity (PO)). Preoperative SVA > 50 mm defined sagittal imbalance; C7-CSVL > 20 mm defined coronal imbalance. Statistical analysis employed paired non-parametric tests and multivariate regression. Results In the 58 patients with preoperative sagittal imbalance (SVA > 50 mm), mean SVA improved significantly from 77.9 mm (SD 24.4) to 59.9 mm (SD 36.1; p < 0.001), with 27.6% (16 out of 58) moving to the sagittal balance group postoperatively. Preoperative SVA was the sole independent predictor of SVA correction (R² 0.25; p = 0.009). In the 41 coronally imbalanced patients, LLD was corrected from 11.4 mm (SD 20.9) to 1.0 mm (SD 14.2; p < 0.001), with 31.7% (17 out of 41) becoming balanced after THA. From standing to deep-seated, there was an increase in PFA change from 48.8° (SD 18.5°) to 54.6° (SD 20.3°; p < 0.001) and reduced anterior pelvic tilt (ΔPT) from 15.8° (SD 14.0°) to 10.3° (SD 14.5°; p < 0.001). Conclusion THA improves global sagittal and coronal spinal imbalance, restoring spinopelvic mobility by increasing hip flexion and reducing compensatory pelvic tilt. These dynamic postoperative changes challenge the static assumptions underpinning current hip-spine classifications. Preoperative and postoperative analysis of global dynamic spinopelvic balance and mobility are crucial for managing hip-spine syndrome. Cite this article: Bone Joint J 2026;108-B(11):1315–1324.

papers.title: A comparison of the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants with low molecular weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Aims To evaluate differences in the efficacy and safety of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) used for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after elective total hip arthroplasty (THA). Methods This systematic review and meta-analysis reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from conception to 13 December 2025, for any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the efficacy (VTE risk) and safety (bleeding risk) of LMWH and DOACs after elective THA. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) of VTE, bleeding, reoperation, and mortality risks were assessed. Results A total of 22 RCTs involving 28,112 participants were included. The risk of VTE in the DOAC group was lower compared with the LMWH group (OR 0.62 (95% CI 0.47 to 0.82); p = 0.002), driven by a reduction in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) risk (OR 0.60 (95% CI 0.42 to 0.86); p = 0.008). The findings remained consistent in the subgroup analysis restricted to anticoagulants and dosages licensed for use in the UK. Overall bleeding risk was higher in the DOAC group (OR 1.19 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.38); p = 0.023), but no difference was seen when comparing only UK-licensed anticoagulants and doses (OR 1.06 (95% CI 0.95 to 1.18); p = 0.279). Reoperation risk (OR 1.21 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.93); p = 0.351) and mortality (OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.46 to 2.33); p = 0.937) did not differ between groups. Conclusion DOACs reduce the risk of VTE and DVT following elective THA compared with LMWH without increasing bleeding risk, for UK-licensed agents and doses. Switching to DOACs could save the NHS £8.6 million per year. New clinical trials are needed to compare the safety and efficacy of UK-licensed DOACs and LWMH with modern postoperative rehabilitation protocols. Cite this article: Bone Joint J 2026;108-B(11):1294–1304.

papers.title: Health-related quality of life following periprosthetic femoral fracture after total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Aims The aim of this study was to quantify the impact of a postoperative periprosthetic femoral fracture following a primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) on patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) compared with normal values in the general population, and to assess the agreement between recalled pre-fracture and prospectively collected PROMs. Methods This single-centre retrospective cohort study involved 140 operatively managed patients with a periprosthetic femoral fracture which was sustained around a primary THA, between 2007 and 2025, with a minimum follow-up of one year. The EQ-5D-3L, EQ-VAS, and Oxford Hip Score (OHS) were collected at a median of 2.9 years (IQR 1.9 to 5.5) after the fracture. Complete case propensity score matching (1:5) balanced patients who had a periprosthetic fracture with Health Survey for England general population controls (n = 700) by sex, age, and deprivation. An agreement cohort with data from a linked arthroplasty database enabled comparison between prospectively collected PROMs one year after THA and recalled pre-fracture PROMs, as well as the analysis of PROMs at four timepoints (before THA, one year after THA, pre-fracture recall, and after the periprosthetic femoral fracture). Results The mean EQ-5D-3L scores after periprosthetic femoral fracture were significantly lower than those in the matched general population (mean difference -0.209 (95% CI -0.264 to -0.154); p < 0.001). Almost two-thirds of patients (62.9%; n = 88) reported a clinically meaningful decrease compared with the general population, with 9.3% (n = 13/140) reporting health states which were worse than death. Subgroup analysis of patients with prospectively collected one-year post-THA and recalled pre-injury PROMs (n = 22) showed good agreement (EQ-5D-3L, intraclass correlation coefficient 0.884 (95% CI 0.746 to 0.950)), with 77.3% (n = 17) being within the minimal important change threshold. Analysis of the trajectory at the four timepoints showed that a periprosthetic femoral fracture had a lasting impact on PROMs, with 38.9% of EQ-5D-3L and 36.4% of the benefit in the OHS being erased following the fracture. Conclusion A periprosthetic femoral fracture following primary THA was associated with a clinically meaningful reduction in PROMs in about two-thirds of patients, with one-in-ten reporting health states worse than death, at a median follow-up of about three years. These findings have important implications when counselling patients and for targeted strategies designed to prevent a periprosthetic femoral fracture. Cite this article: Bone Joint J 2026;108-B(11):1335–1343.

papers.title: Outcomes of a long modular uncemented femoral stem for reconstruction in metastatic femoral disease
papers.abstract: Aims Cemented arthroplasty has previously been recommended for treating metastatic bone disease (MBD) around the hip. However, cementing has disadvantages, including restricted femoral component length, loosening due to disease progression, and bone cement implantation syndrome (BCIS). A long uncemented implant spanning the whole femur could negate these disadvantages; however, there is a paucity of data regarding their use. Our aim was to assess the outcomes of a long uncemented femoral component in MBD. Methods A total of 205 patients with MBD underwent femoral reconstruction using the Restoration Modular Revision Hip System Plasma stem between January 2008 and December 2025. They were identified from the prospectively collected database of a tertiary MBD service. Any patient with symptomatic bone metastases involving the acetabulum or femur, with completed or impending pathological fracture, were included. The primary endpoint was reintervention for femoral implant failure, with exclusion of reintervention for deep infection and/or instability. Results Indications for surgery included pathological fracture (46 of 205; 22%) or lesions at risk of fracture (78%; n = 159). The mean follow-up was 45 months (12 to 131). A total of 140 patients (68%) died during the study period (mean 20 months (0.1 to 128) postoperatively). The mean distance from the centre of the femoral head to the most distal femoral metastasis was 126 mm (5 to 369). Using death as a competing risk, two-year probability of reintervention was 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025) and probability of death was 0.507 (95% CI 0.436 to 0.577). At five years, probability of reintervention was 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025) and the risk of death was 0.703 (95% CI 0.629 to 0.776). Overall complication rate requiring further surgery was 8% (16 out of 205) with three reinterventions for femoral implant failure (all periprosthetic femoral fractures). Conclusion This implant demonstrates promising short- to mid-term survivorship, with no patient requiring femoral revision for loosening and a comparatively low complication rate. A long uncemented femoral component may be an appropriate option in selected patients presenting with symptomatic bone metastases around the hip. Cite this article: Bone Joint J 2026;108-B(11):1344–1353.

papers.title: ML Technique Provides Hybrid Framework for Multiphase-Flow Measurement
papers.abstract: _ This article, written by JPT Technology Editor Chris Carpenter, contains highlights of paper SPE 228033, “Advancing Multiphase Flow Measurement: Machine Learning vs. Traditional MPFM in Flow-Loop Testing,” by Henry Qi Jin and Willow Liu, SPE, Medeng. The paper has not been peer-reviewed. _ This study demonstrates the transformative potential of physics-informed neural networks as a hybrid framework for multiphase flow measurement. A physics-informed neural network (PINN) was developed to solve the complex Navier-Stokes equations for multiphase flow measurement, including flow rates of individual phases in the multiphase mixture and phase ratios. The results were compared with a mathematics-based multiphase-flow-measurement approach and validated through a controlled loop test using oil, water, and gas. The PINN reduced reliance on predefined correlations and offered greater adaptability to changing fluid properties. The repeatability of results confirmed the model’s reliability, positioning PINNs as a promising alternative for complex multiphase-flow-measurement applications. Result To evaluate the performance of the proposed PINN for multiphase-flow-rate estimation, its predictions were compared with those from a mathematical-model-based multiphase flowmeter (MPFM) and the ground-truth values obtained from the high-temperature flow loop. The comparisons were structured into three categories to better understand the behavior of the PINN under varying flow conditions: variation in water cut, variation in gas volume fraction (GVF), and variation in total mass flow rate. For each category, multiple test cases were conducted to ensure consistency and validate the repeatability of the PINN’s performance.

papers.title: THREE-DIMENSIONAL PRINTING IN PHARMACEUTICS AND HEALTHCARE: TECHNOLOGIES, APPLICATIONS, PERSONALIZED MEDICINE AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing or three-dimensional (3D) printing is an emerging technology in pharmaceutical and medical industries. It allows for the layer-by-layer creation of dosage forms with tailored shape, drug loading, internal architecture, and release characteristics, in contrast to traditional manufacture. This review discusses the essential ideas and workflow of 3D printing, including computer-aided design, STL conversion, slicing, fabrication, and post-processing. Major printing technologies, such as fused deposition modeling, stereolithography, digital light processing, continuous liquid interface production, selective laser sintering, selective laser melting, semi-solid extrusion, and inkjet printing, are reviewed with emphasis on their operating mechanisms, advantages, limitations, and pharmaceutical relevance. Applications in pediatric and geriatric formulations, patient-specific dosage, polypills, immediate-, sustained-, and pulsatile-release systems, osmotic systems, and 3D-printed microneedles are also highlighted in the review. The review also addresses ethical and regulatory considerations related to sterility, material safety, process validation, quality control, and patient safety. Overall, 3D printing represents a versatile platform for customized and controlled drug delivery; however, material limitations, scalability, safety, and regulatory challenges remain important barriers to broader clinical translation.

papers.title: AI DRIVEN DIGITAL TWINS FOR DRUG REPURPOSING: CURRENT EVIDENCES, APPLICATIONS, TRANSLATIONAL CHALLENGES AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS
papers.abstract: Conventional drug discovery and development is associated with substantial financial costs, lengthy development timelines, and high attrition rates during preclinical and clinical evaluation. Drug repurposing provides an alternative strategy by identifying new therapeutic applications for existing drugs with previously characterized pharmacological and safety profiles. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, multimodal biomedical data integration, mechanistic modelling, and digital twin technology have created new opportunities to improve computational drug repurposing and patient-specific treatment prediction. This review examines the emerging integration of AI-driven digital twins with drug repurposing, focusing on digital twin architectures, artificial intelligence methodologies multi modal data integration, drug target prediction, pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic modelling, treatment-response simulation, and personalized therapeutic decision-making. The review also discusses applications across cancer, neurodegenerative, cardiovascular, infectious, metabolic, and rare diseases. Particular emphasis is placed on the development of patient-specific digital twins, integration of multi-omics and clinical data, virtual treatment simulation, and validation through computational, experimental, and clinical approaches. Major challenges include data heterogeneity, interoperability, model reliability, uncertainty quantification, interpretability, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity, privacy, clinical workflow integration, and regulatory acceptance. Emerging approaches, including causal AI, federated learning, multimodal foundation models, virtual clinical trials, and real-time adaptive digital twins, may further enhance the translational potential of AI-enabled drug repurposing. However, prospective clinical validation and standardized regulatory frameworks remain necessary before widespread clinical implementation.

papers.title: Clinical outcomes of transposition osteotomy of the acetabulum in patients aged 50 years or older with hip dysplasia
papers.abstract: Aims To clarify whether transposition osteotomy of the acetabulum (TOA) in patients aged ≥ 50 years with hip dysplasia provides clinical, radiological, and patient-reported outcomes comparable with those in younger patients. Methods Among 615 patients undergoing TOA between November 1998 and July 2019, 131 patients aged ≥ 50 years were propensity score-matched 1:1 to 131 patients aged < 50 years using sex, BMI, preoperative modified Harris Hip Score (mHHS), Tönnis grade, and lateral centre-edge angle. Matching was repeated with controls aged < 45 years. Clinical and radiological outcomes, joint survival, and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were compared. Failure was defined as progression to Tönnis grade 3 osteoarthritis or conversion to total hip arthroplasty. Predictors of failure in patients aged ≥ 50 years were examined using Cox regression. Results In patients aged ≥ 50 years, the median mHHS improved from 62 (IQR 54 to 75) to 92 (IQR 84 to 96) (p < 0.001), with scores comparable with those in patients aged < 50 years (p = 0.685). Failure occurred in seven (5.3%) and ten hips (7.6%), respectively (p = 0.607), with similar ten- and 20-year joint survival (98% (95% CI 94 to 100) and 79% (95% CI 55 to 91) vs 97% (95% CI 89 to 99) and 72% (95% CI 51 to 86); p = 0.655). PROMs did not differ significantly between groups. When compared with patients aged < 45 years, patients aged ≥ 50 years had a lower median Hip disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score sport/recreation score (75 (IQR 56 to 81) vs 81 (IQR 63 to 94); p = 0.044) and more complications (12 (9.2%) vs 2 (1.5%); p = 0.013). Preoperative Tönnis grade 2 independently predicted failure (hazard ratio 8.67 (95% CI 1.36 to 55.34); p = 0.022). Conclusion TOA achieved long-term joint survival comparable with that in younger patients, supporting TOA as a joint-preserving option in this age group. However, the sport/recreation score was lower and complications more frequent than in patients aged < 45 years. Preoperative Tönnis grade 2 predicted failure, indicating that joint degeneration, rather than age alone, should guide patient selection. Cite this article: Bone Joint J 2026;108-B(11):1305–1314.

papers.title: Polymeric Biomaterials with Multiple Stratified Layers for Periodontal Ligament/Bone Regeneration: A Review.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic pathological condition initiated by bacterial plaque accumulation and characterized by the progressive destruction of the tooth-supporting tissues, including the periodontal ligament, cementum, and alveolar bone. If left untreated, it may result in tooth mobility, pathologic tooth migration, and ultimately tooth loss. Despite numerous regenerative strategies, complete periodontal regeneration remains challenging. Guided tissue regeneration (GTR) and guided bone regeneration (GBR) promote the regeneration of the periodontal ligament and alveolar bone; however, current GTR/GBR biomaterials often exhibit inadequate mechanical stability and osseointegration. To overcome these limitations, various multilayer biomaterials with enhanced functionalities have been developed. This review outlines the key properties required for GTR/GBR, evaluates the design and performance of current multilayer biomaterials, and examines their major limitations, particularly their inability to fully replicate native periodontal tissues due to structural incompatibilities between layers. Finally, future directions and recommendations are presented to guide the development of next-generation GTR/GBR biomaterials.

papers.title: Mixed‐Scale Powder Enables 3D Printing of Tungsten Alloy
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) offers a promising route for manufacturing tungsten alloy components with complex geometries, whereas W–Ni–Fe alloys remain the most widely used tungsten alloys because of their excellent overall performance. Using nano‐sized Ni–Fe particles can further promote the densification and strengthening of LPBF‐fabricated W–Ni–Fe parts. However, nano‐enabled W–Ni–Fe powders face a critical trade‐off between reinforcing‐phase content and powder‐bed quality of LPBF: although a higher Ni–Fe content is generally beneficial for performance enhancement, excessive nanoparticles tend to deteriorate powder flowability and thereby impair powder‐bed uniformity during LPBF. Here, we propose a mixed‐scale nano/micron Ni–Fe/W powder design to overcome this dilemma and enable the fabrication of fine‐grained, high‐quality W–Ni–Fe parts by LPBF, thereby providing an alternative mixed‐scale strategy for reinforcing‐phase design. Compared with conventional mono‐scale nano Ni–Fe/W powder, the mixed‐scale powder promotes pronounced grain refinement, resulting in an average grain size of 4.90 μm. Meanwhile, it significantly improves both the forming quality and mechanical performance, achieving a surface roughness ( S a ) of 7.56 μm, a compressive strength of 2534.2 MPa, and a compressive strain of 34.1%. This work provides an engineering‐feasible powder design strategy and processing pathway for the LPBF fabrication of high‐performance tungsten alloys, and may also be extended to the additive manufacturing of other refractory metals that face a similar trade‐off between reinforcement content and powder flowability.

papers.abstract: Although the active learning model has been widely implemented in Islamic Religious Education (PAI) learning, studies that specifically examine its implementation from the perspective of Vygotsky’s constructivism at SMAN 1 Narmada remain limited. This study aims to analyze the implementation of the active learning model in PAI learning based on the perspective of Vygotsky’s constructivism and to identify the supporting and inhibiting factors in its implementation. This study used a qualitative approach with a field research design involving PAI teachers and Grade X students as research subjects selected purposively. Data were collected through observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation, then analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, which includes data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing. The results show that the implementation of active learning was carried out through group discussion, question-and-answer, presentation, information search, case study, and card sort strategies. The implementation of this model is aligned with Vygotsky’s constructivism, particularly through the concepts of the Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) and scaffolding, which emphasize collaboration, social interaction, and learning assistance. The research findings show that active learning supports increased student engagement, material comprehension, critical thinking skills, communication skills, and cooperation in PAI learning. The supporting factors for implementation include the availability of learning technology facilities, the use of digital media, and positive social interaction among students, whereas the inhibiting factors include limited facilities and infrastructure, low self-confidence among some students in expressing opinions, and classroom management that is not yet optimal. The conclusion of the study affirms that the active learning model from the perspective of Vygotsky’s constructivism plays an important role in creating active, contextual, collaborative, and meaningful PAI learning. The implications of this study provide theoretical contributions to the development of constructivism-based PAI learning studies, as well as practical implications for teachers in designing learning strategies that are more participatory and responsive to students’ learning needs.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence applied to formulation design, process optimization, and quality assessment of 3D-printed dosage forms and drug-delivery systems: a scoping review
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) printing is a computer-aided, layer-by-layer manufacturing technology with strong potential for personalized medicines. Combined with artificial intelligence (AI), it enables predictive, data-driven development, improving formulation design, process robustness, and quality control. However, evidence remains fragmented across technologies, dosage forms, and computational approaches. This scoping review aimed to map and describe the application of AI to formulation design, manufacturing-process optimization, and quality assessment of pharmaceutical dosage forms and drug-delivery systems produced by 3D printing, including device-assisted delivery systems such as microneedles. The review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were conducted in MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science until November 18, 2025. Original studies applying AI to the design, manufacturing, or quality assessment of 3D-printed drug products or drug–device combinations were included. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and analysis. Findings were synthesized through descriptive tables and narrative analysis. Twenty studies published between 2020 and 2025 met the inclusion criteria. Technologies included Fused Deposition Modeling, Selective Laser Sintering, Semi-Solid Extrusion, Vat Photopolymerization, and Inkjet Printing. Oral dosage forms and associated formulation or printing workflows predominated; two studies specifically investigated microneedle-based delivery systems. Reported approaches included random forests, support vector machines, artificial neural networks, deep learning, chemometric regression, generative models, Bayesian optimization, and evolutionary algorithms. Applications addressed formulation and printability prediction, processing-condition selection, drug-release modeling, and image-based quality assessment. Individual studies reported potential benefits related to process robustness, experimental effort, and development time; however, differences in study designs, datasets, and outcome definitions limit comparisons and generalization. The review maps applications of AI in formulation design, process optimization, and quality assessment in pharmaceutical 3D printing, without establishing their comparative effectiveness. Future research should prioritize methodological harmonization, standardized validation, and interdisciplinary collaboration to facilitate translation and regulatory acceptance.

papers.title: Leakage-safe and uncertainty-aware surrogate modelling for mechanistic tensile strain prediction in flexible pavements
papers.abstract: Mechanistic pavement analysis relies on accurate prediction of critical structural responses, particularly tensile strain at the bottom of the asphalt layer (εt), obtained from multilayer elastic analysis. Repeated mechanistic simulations, however, can become computationally demanding in large parametric studies, optimisation, and reliability assessment. This study develops and validates an engineering-oriented surrogate modelling framework for rapid prediction of KENPAVE-generated tensile strain within a predefined structural–loading domain. A canonical dataset of 2,076 simulations was evaluated using leakage-safe five-fold GroupKFold validation with 1,887 independent validation groups. Support Vector Regression with a radial basis function kernel provided the best performance, achieving an out-of-fold R² of 0.99833 and MAPE of 1.501%. The framework also integrates empirical residual-based uncertainty quantification and domain-of-applicability assessment. Prediction intervals achieved coverage close to the nominal 95% level in well-supported regions, while reduced reliability was identified in low-support regions. The surrogate substantially reduced computational time, enabling efficient parametric exploration, optimisation, and reliability analysis. The approach is intended to accelerate mechanistic response evaluation within the defined simulation domain rather than serve as a universal fatigue-performance prediction model.

papers.title: Bathymetry Estimations Using Self Adaptive-Physics Informed Neural Networks on Two Dimensional Shallow Water Equations
papers.abstract: For applications in geophysical research, coastal hazard forecasting, and marine navigation, accurate bathymetry estimation is essential. Even though they work well, conventional methods like satellite remote sensing and shipborne sonar are still costly and restricted in areas with few measurements. In this work, we assess an inverse problem of bathymetry reconstruction from two-dimensional shallow water equations using a Self-Adaptive Physics-Informed Neural Network (SA-PINN) framework. Through dynamically weighted loss terms, the model combines physical constraints with data fidelity. Five-run ablation studies show that reconstruction accuracy depends on both the network architecture and the selected loss-weight configuration. The trainable weighting mechanism provides empirical loss rescaling, while the fixed-weight experiments demonstrate sensitivity to the prescribed penalty ratio. Furthermore, we evaluate the architectural impact of Fourier feature embeddings against standard network topologies for resolving spectral topographic frequencies. To assess the framework’s reliance on ground-truth data, we conduct a sparsity ablation down to 0.1% spatial anchors and an anchor-free configuration. Reconstruction error increases substantially as bathymetry supervision is reduced, indicating continued dependence on direct bathymetric information. Finally, controlled finite-difference perturbations are used to examine the local numerical sensitivity of the trained reconstruction procedure. The resulting terms describe the response at the selected perturbation magnitude and adaptation protocol.

papers.abstract: Thai adolescents are increasingly exposed to violent and sexual content in digital media, which may shape attitudes and increase risk behaviors. This experimental study evaluated whether an active learning-based media literacy program could improve media literacy skills, violence avoidance skills, and sexual risk prevention skills among Thai adolescents. A two-group pretest-posttest design was used with 114 students aged 14-16 years in Chonburi Province, Thailand, who were assigned to either an experimental group or a control group. The experimental group received five 50-minute active learning sessions over five weeks, while the control group received lecture-based instruction. Data were collected using a validated questionnaire and analyzed with paired-samples and independent-samples t-tests. At baseline, the two groups did not differ significantly in media literacy skills, violence avoidance skills, or sexual risk prevention skills. After the intervention, the experimental group had significantly higher mean scores than the control group for media literacy skills (3.97 ± 0.52 vs. 3.10 ± 0.78, p < 0.001), violence avoidance skills (3.48 ± 0.70 vs. 3.11 ± 0.51, p = 0.002), and sexual risk prevention skills (3.78 ± 0.46 vs. 2.90 ± 0.65, p < 0.001). These findings indicate that active learning can effectively strengthen media literacy and support protective behaviors related to violence and sexual risk among adolescents. The program may be suitable for integration into school-based health education to promote responsible media use and adolescent risk prevention.

papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as key players in skin biology, mediating intercellular communication across diverse physiological and pathological contexts. We explore the mechanistic contributions of EVs derived from skin, emphasizing their influence on immune modulation, senescence and tissue regeneration. We also examine their potential as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic agents, while addressing key technical and conceptual challenges that limit clinical translation. Drawing on collaborative insights from the COST Action NETSKINMODELS, we provide a set of recommendations to advance the field, including standardizing separation protocols, improving functional characterization and integrating with emerging technologies such as microneedles and 3D bioprinting. Together, these perspectives outline a strategic framework for unlocking the diagnostic and therapeutic potential of EVs in dermatological research and clinical care.

papers.title: When to Probe and When to Act: Clarity-Aware Risk-Adaptive Control for Interactive Driving
papers.abstract: Safe navigation in interactive traffic requires autonomous vehicles to reason about unobservable human characteristics and the reciprocal nature of multi-agent interactions. Traditional architectures often decouple prediction from planning, leading to the "Frozen Robot Problem" or unsafe maneuvers under high ambiguity because they treat risk assessment and information acquisition as independent objectives. We argue that the notion of safety should not remain static but must instead dynamically co-evolve with the system's internal confidence: the robot should actively clarify ambiguity when necessary while also recognizing the diminishing returns of information, and naturally transition toward task execution. We introduce a unified belief-space Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework that couples multistep information planning with a clarity-adaptive Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) barrier mechanism. By treating clarity, a scalar informational state, as an explicit planning variable, the controller co-designs its probing strategy with its safety specification, tightening conservatism under high ambiguity and relaxing constraints as confidence improves. We further provide a performance analysis showing that the cost of information seeking and the expected planning-cost gap to a controller that knows the true human characteristic are bounded by residual ambiguity and solver error. We evaluate the framework in lane-merging and unsignalized-intersection scenarios against representative interactive-planning baselines. Across 5,000 simulations, the proposed method achieves the highest success rates (94.6% and 93.2%) and the lowest collision rates (1.2% and 1.4%) among the compared methods, providing a principled foundation for robust decision-making in human-centric environments.

papers.title: Mesh2Shell Neural Operator for Inverse Shape Optimization
papers.abstract: Physics-driven design seeks high-performing geometries, which need not conform to a learned shape category. Parametric and latent-space approaches facilitate surrogate-based optimization, but restrict deformations to prescribed shape families or learned decoders. We introduce the Mesh-to-Shell Neural Operator (M2S-NO) as the mesh-to-shell component of a category-agnostic inverse shape optimization framework. We separate the explicit mesh used for design from the volumetric representation used for physics prediction. M2S-NO maps oriented surface samples to a surface-centered shell representation, such as TruncatedSDF or HeatSDF. A separate problem-specific PDE neural operator (PDE-NO) maps this representation to physical fields. Objective gradients update mesh vertices through both operators, without a latent shape decoder. Preconditioning and remeshing support free-form deformation, while fixed interfaces are controlled directly on the mesh. Optional shell-space proposals enable topology changes. We evaluate geometric matching, jet-engine brackets, and neutron moderators, with independent FEM and OpenMC evaluation. Relative to the best training designs, M2S-NO reduces maximum bracket displacement by 14.3% and increases neutron-sensor current by 13.8%. Optimization also succeeds from an out-of-distribution bracket initialization, demonstrating the framework's geometric flexibility.

papers.title: Black Hole Love Numbers with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We develop and validate a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for computing the tidal Love numbers of black holes directly from their perturbation equations. We consider static perturbations of the Kerr black hole, whose exact hypergeometric solutions provide a controlled benchmark for both the numerical solver and the extraction of the physical response. The framework combines exact enforcement of the horizon boundary conditions with an $H^2$-Sobolev loss that incorporates derivatives of the differential-equation residual. The Love number is then obtained by extracting the asymptotic coefficients of the learned solution, without using the analytic connection formula. Across the tested scalar, vector, and tensor perturbations, the method recovers the finite dissipative response with relative errors below $10^{-5}$. Controlled comparisons show that the higher-derivative loss terms improve solution accuracy by orders of magnitude, while independent tests of the extraction procedure distinguish solver errors from errors in recovering the response coefficients. The conservative response, which vanishes analytically, is constrained by the numerical error floor. These results demonstrate that PINNs can accurately compute black-hole tidal response and establish a validated framework for future extensions to frequency-dependent and non-separable perturbation problems.

papers.title: Rare Event Constrained Reinforcement Learning with Large Deviations
papers.abstract: We study finite-horizon reinforcement learning with a safety constraint on the probability of reaching a failure set. In contrast to the well-studied safe reinforcement learning literature, we consider problems where the probability of reaching the failure set is vanishingly small, but the consequences of reaching the failure set are catastrophic. Direct simulation and estimation of the optimal policy is naturally ineffective when the failure probability is extremely small. Moreover, on a real system the controller can only choose actions, and this is not enough to make failures frequent. In contrast to the rare event simulation literature, our goal is not to estimate the probability of the rare event occurrence, but to upper bound it such that the failure constraint is satisfied. Thus, instead of sampling failures, we use the large deviations principle. We define a damage variable that on exceeding a certain threshold indicates failure. We study the cumulant generating function (CGF) as its positive root provides an upper bound on the failure probability via Cramer's theorem. We extend this approach to Markov decision processes with hitting times through state-action CGFs, and give finite-horizon and state-dependent versions of the bound. The state-action CGFs do not depend on the policy and can be estimated from regular transitions, so the bound can be checked for any policy a priori. This gives a policy improvement algorithm in which every policy satisfies the failure constraint with high probability.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning in High-Energy Physics: A Survey from Accelerator Control to Theory Exploration
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a machine learning paradigm in which an agent learns a decision-making policy by interacting with an environment, guided by a scalar reward rather than explicit supervision. Supervised and unsupervised learning have become indispensable tools in high-energy physics (HEP), but they learn from fixed datasets, whereas many HEP tasks are closed-loop decisions: the data an algorithm observes depend on its choices, the feedback is sparse or delayed, and the objective is often measured on a real machine or in a stochastic simulation, not by a differentiable model. This survey reviews the application of RL to such tasks: accelerator control and feedback, data quality monitoring, jet grooming, clustering, and representation, charged particle tracking, beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) and string model building, detector design, trigger control, analysis, and formal quantum field theory computation. It provides a self-contained introduction to the underlying RL methods, from model-free and model-based to multi-agent, offline, inverse, and bandit approaches, reviews each domain against its traditional methods, and summarizes the head-to-head comparisons. The applications range from policies deployed on real accelerators and evaluated on recorded collision data to exploratory studies in formal theory. RL is most advantageous for repeated tasks with a fast simulator, decisions inside fast control loops, operation under faults and corrupted measurements, physics-based rewards in place of labels, and sequential discrete constructions with a reusable policy, while Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithms, and differentiable methods remain competitive elsewhere. We conclude with the open challenges that recur across domains, including reward design, sim-to-real transfer, safety, the lack of shared benchmarks, and the statistical validity of policy-driven decisions.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware 3D Position Reconstruction in CZT Drift-Strip Detectors
papers.abstract: Accurate three-dimensional interaction-position reconstruction is important for CZT drift-strip detectors, but conventional methods can suffer from degraded performance in challenging detector regions, while learned models provide limited information about prediction reliability. We investigate two uncertainty-aware approaches: deep ensembles of point-estimation networks and simulation-based inference (SBI), which estimates a posterior distribution over interaction position. Both approaches are trained on physics-based simulations and evaluated on both synthetic and experimental data. On synthetic data, uncertainty from both methods correlates with positioning error, with SBI showing a substantially stronger relationship. On experimental measurements, the deep ensemble achieves improved $z$-position resolution, while SBI provides more informative uncertainty estimates that highlight regions of reduced positional information and discrepancies between simulation and the physical detector. These results demonstrate the complementary strengths of ensemble-based reconstruction and posterior inference for uncertainty-aware detector position reconstruction.

papers.title: RubricWorld: World Model-Guided Rubric Optimization for LLM Graders
papers.abstract: Rubric optimization improves LLM grading by revising scoring instructions while keeping the grader's parameters fixed. Existing optimizers often judge edits by aggregate validation performance, limiting the supervision they retain about which errors an edit corrects or introduces. Testing each candidate also requires rescoring validation answers, which limits how many edits can be explored within a fixed budget. We propose RubricWorld, a framework that learns from previous edit evaluations to guide further search. Its world model predicts an edit's correction and degradation rates at score boundaries, conditioned on the current rubric state. The training signal comes from paired grading results: scores for the same answers before and after an edit. Predictions select one candidate for direct evaluation, and held-out confidence bounds determine whether it corrects enough target errors while keeping new errors within prespecified limits. Measured effects update the model even when the edit is rejected. Across EIR (National), ASAP2.0, and ASAP-SAS with three frozen LLM graders, RubricWorld achieves the highest score in 20 of 27 metric comparisons. On ASAP2.0, it raises gpt-5-mini accuracy from 18.20% with the original rubric to 46.70%, exceeding the strongest baseline, APO, by 22.60 percentage points. code will be released upon acceptance.

papers.title: Large-Scale Bayesian Optimisation Using Uncertainty-Calibrated Product-of-Experts Gaussian Process Models with Trust Regions
papers.abstract: The use of collections of independent local Gaussian processes (GP-ind) combined with trust regions is a widely adopted approach for large-scale and high-dimensional Bayesian optimisation (BO). However, this approach suffers from several limitations, including discontinuities at the boundaries of disjoint regions, an inability to capture long-range spatial correlations, potential information loss, and abrupt increases in computational overhead. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel BO algorithm, termed BO-pro-c-tr. The proposed method employs a product-of-experts Gaussian process model with uncertainty calibration (GP-pro-c) as its surrogate model and incorporates a one-to-many association strategy for integrating GP-pro-c with trust regions. Empirical results suggest that, when combined with the GP-LCB acquisition function, BO-pro-c-tr achieves an average reduction of 2.6% in simple regret and 34.9% in computational overhead relative to BO algorithms based on independent local GP models coupled with trust regions.

papers.title: Online Active Learning Architecture for Safety-Critical Control Systems
papers.abstract: The transition of information-centric artificial intelligence to safety-critical applications is impeded by the limitations of conventional offline-training paradigms in open-world environments. This paper presents Control AI, an architecture for Online Active Learning (OAL) inspired by the continuous Prediction-Evaluation-Correction process of biological intelligence. The framework combines the hierarchical representation capacity of deep neural networks with the real-time error-feedback adaptation of adaptive control. A prediction model maps sensory input into a latent manifold, an optional latent model represents transitions in that space, and a reconstruction model maps the latent state back to observable signals. Residuals between predictions and measurements provide the internal learning signal. Spatial and temporal cross-reconstruction architectures prevent OAL from collapsing to a trivial identity mapping, while coupled, dual, and localized variants shorten error-transmission paths. Localized predictive coding style OAL is implemented through guidance-backpropagation and target-backpropagation architectures, and hybrid and scaled variants support high-dimensional deployment. The paper focuses on the architectural rationale and the progression from a conceptual feedback loop to practical large-scale configurations.

papers.title: Robust Remote ECG Monitoring under Energy Constraints: Anomaly Filtering versus Predictive Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Machine learning for remote electrocardiogram monitoring must handle noise and diseases absent from training under tight resource constraints. We investigate whether upstream unsupervised anomaly detection can improve monitoring decisions more efficiently than classifier-derived uncertainty. We evaluate five detectors on PTB-XL and BUT QDB and compare a two-stage filter-classifier system with Monte Carlo Dropout and deep ensembles under unseen-disease and noise conditions. Performance is averaged over five training seeds. We measure single-pass energy, latency, and graph memory on a microcontroller's central processing unit (CPU) and neural processing unit (NPU). Per-score neural network costs account for repeated evaluations but exclude scoring outside deployed graphs. Energy equations relate filtering and rejection to avoided classifier execution. Across four disease scenarios, Deep Support Vector Data Description (Deep SVDD) achieves the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve within all tested finite CPU energy budgets. On the NPU, it leads at 1 mJ, while Monte Carlo Dropout has slightly higher means at 10 and 100 mJ. With a narrow CPU classifier, the Deep SVDD two-stage system increases the fraction of correctly classified or correctly rejected inputs by 15.0-19.4 percentage points over classification without rejection. Estimated energy per input is 1.93-6.99 mJ, compared with 52.53 mJ for Monte Carlo Dropout and 8.76-17.51 mJ for deep ensembles, at each method's retrospectively selected test accuracy peak. These results support upstream filtering for efficient remote monitoring, while independent validation and complete-system measurements remain necessary.

papers.title: The (Butter)fly Dream: Linear Separability of World-Model Rollouts in a Connectome-Constrained Visual Model
papers.abstract: Zhuangzi dreamt he was a butterfly and, on waking, could not tell which was the dream. We ask a version of his question of a model of the fly brain: placed inside a world generated by a world model, can a fixed brain tell that the world is a dream? We treat it as a question about what a connectome-constrained model trained on one task makes available beyond that task: do its responses make the defects of a dream linearly decodable? The observer is a published model of the fly visual system trained only for optic-flow estimation; reality is the MPI-Sintel movie on the model's 721-column retina; dreams are continuations of five real frames by three small world models (a persistence random walk, an MDN-RNN and an RSSM) at three temperatures. The judge is a classifier two-sample test on temporal statistics of cell-type responses, with sequence-level cross-validation. In the trained observer's responses all nine dreams are separable from reality (AUC 0.85-0.99, mean over 50 trained models), in those of the same network before training much less so (0.58-0.75 for the learned world models; paired difference 0.20-0.37), equally on sequences the observer never saw, and in an order unrelated to pixel error. Because these AUCs are near ceiling, we add graded probes made of each window's own real frames with only their order broken. Swapping one adjacent pair of the 14 generated frames gives 0.73 on the trained responses against 0.54 before training and 0.56 for pixel statistics; the trained curve reaches 0.75 at 1.1 swapped pairs of seven, the pixel statistics at 4.7, and the untrained network not at all. A detection horizon, the test on the first k generated frames, orders the world models where the full-length AUC saturates.

papers.title: OpenNWM: A Generalist Navigation World Model with Latent Action Pretraining
papers.abstract: Navigation world models predict future observations conditioned on navigation actions to support planning, but their generalization across real-world environments remains constrained by the limited coverage of action-labeled data. Action-free navigation videos provide diverse visual experience, yet lack the recorded actions required for action-conditioned training. We introduce OpenNWM, a generalist navigation world model with latent action pretraining. It learns universal latent actions from large-scale action-free videos through visual prediction pretraining, and further aligns them with physical motions via action-conditioned post-training. To support video pretraining, we curate NavAnywhere, a large-scale action-free navigation video dataset comprising 17.5 million visual observations from 15 heterogeneous sources. It captures navigation by ground robots, humans, and drones, with diverse viewpoints and motion patterns across five broad scene types: residential areas, public and commercial spaces, urban settings, parks, and natural landscapes. Experiments demonstrate improved visual prediction on in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, together with improved navigation performance. These results show that latent-action pretraining enables diverse, action-free videos to improve dynamics learning and generalization for open-world navigation.

papers.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Real-Time Electric Vehicle Charging Management in IoEV-Enabled Smart Cities
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) in urban environments demands intelligent, decentralised charging management strategies that operate under strict real-time constraints. This paper proposes an Edge-Intelligent architecture in which each EV selects a charging station (CS) by querying a shared, centrally trained Deep Q-Network (DQN) policy over a lightweight MQTT publish-subscribe backbone; independent per-EV edge inference is the deployment target, not the configuration evaluated here. The reported simulation evaluates that shared DQN policy applied sequentially to each vehicle's observations within a single SUMO run, using MQTT for KPI telemetry while observations are obtained through TraCI. The system is evaluated on two real-world road networks from OpenStreetMap (Rabat Agdal-Hay Riad and Tangier, Morocco); the primary network carries four geolocated public charging stations with heterogeneous power levels (50 kW and 150 kW). Three traffic demand profiles (morning, midday, evening peak) are simulated, and four decision policies are compared: an Adaptive Heuristic, a Tabular Q-Learning agent, the proposed DQN agent, and a Double DQN variant. A multi-seed statistical protocol (7 seeds, Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Cohen's d) evaluates the results. The DQN agent achieves a 6.8% relative improvement in charge rate and a 5.4% increase in delivered energy over the Adaptive Heuristic under Evening Peak demand ($p = 0.016$, Cohen's $d = 0.99$ and $1.51$), while showing no advantage in waiting time; on the second network the heuristic leads on waiting time, so the ranking is not stable across geographies. A scalability analysis shows linear state-space growth with station count and sub-millisecond inference; all runs include intermittent station outages under a Markov failure process.

papers.title: Robust EEG-based Emotion Recognition from Coarse Trial-level Labels under Intra-trial Affective Variability
papers.abstract: EEG-based emotion recognition has become an active research area in brain-computer interfaces. However, fine-grained affective annotation is costly, so most datasets provide only a global label for each long EEG trial. For practical emotion recognition, trials are commonly divided into short temporal windows, with the global label propagated to all windows for training. This practice treats trial-level emotion as temporally uniform, although affective responses may fluctuate within a trial. Consequently, windows that weakly reflect or deviate from the global emotional state may receive unreliable labels, posing a key challenge to robust EEG-based emotion recognition. To address this challenge, we propose VARY, a variability-aware robust learning framework for EEG-based emotion recognition from coarse trial-level labels. VARY incorporates a Two-stage Sample Selection (TSS) strategy to identify EEG windows with reliable emotional labels, and introduces MixAug, a data augmentation method tailored for EEG to improve model robustness under limited and unreliable supervision. We comprehensively evaluate VARY under the setting of label-noise learning on two public datasets, using three network architectures and multiple label-noise settings. Our method demonstrates superior performance, achieving a maximum accuracy gain of 11.54% on the DREAMER dataset and 5.39% on the SEED dataset compared with the best-performing baseline, highlighting the effectiveness of VARY in learning from unreliable trial-level labels under intra-trial affective variability.

papers.title: ODE Policy: Robot Learning via Action Dynamics, Not Actions
papers.abstract: Most robot policies, whether trained by imitation learning (IL) or reinforcement learning (RL), map observations to action values at discrete control steps and leave the continuity of physical motion to be learned implicitly. We propose ODE policy, which learns the dynamics of the action rather than the action itself. A neural ordinary differential equation (ODE) learns the vector field of the action by matching the integrated actions to the targets over short action chunks in IL and single control steps in RL. A lightweight diversity head captures multi-modal behavior by randomizing the direction of the field. At deployment, each action is integrated from the previous one, so the executed trajectory is continuous by construction. We evaluate it as a visuomotor policy, as the action head of vision-language-action (VLA) and world action models (WAMs), and as the actor of model-based RL against 14 baselines on unimanual, bimanual, dexterous, locomotion, and loco-manipulation tasks. In IL, against flow matching, it reaches 5.9$\times$ the success, 5.4$\times$ the generalization, and 3.9$\times$ the mode balance after one epoch, and generates actions 10.8$\times$ faster. It mostly moves more smoothly than human demonstrations. On 14 real-world tasks across single-arm, dual-arm, dexterous, and humanoid robots, it achieves the highest success rate. In RL, it further speeds up SuperMimic for humanoid motion tracking and smooths its actions. Efficient in learning, data, parameters, and execution, ODE policy offers a promising path to scaling robot learning.

papers.title: Beyond Imputation: Mask-Adaptive Conformal Prediction via Tree Embeddings on General Missing Data Mechanisms
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction (CP) provides a distribution-free framework for uncertainty quantification with finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees. Yet, missing values introduce distributional heterogeneity, where marginal coverage can hide systematic undercoverage for certain missingness patterns. At the same time, existing methods based on distances or smoothness require a continuous representation of partially observed covariates. Although imputation restores continuity, it obscures the missingness patterns and introduces task-dependent overhead. We develop a new CP framework that is \emph{adaptive to missingness patterns}, without imputing covariates. We rely on data augmentation by feature embedding that accounts for missingness. Our framework represents each input with missing values by a tree embedding together with its raw missingness mask, and then learns a regularized quantile score function. Varying the choices for the penalty function and the augmentation enables us to characterize three practically relevant validity levels: exact coordinate-wise validity, exact validity on observed masks, and approximate missingness-conditional guarantees for general mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR). Experiments on synthetic and real datasets support these guarantees and show that the proposed method reduces miscoverage risk while maintaining informative intervals, especially in non-MCAR settings. These results highlight the practical value of uncertainty quantification that adapts to missingness.

papers.title: A sensor-driven physics-informed neural network for real-time occupant-centric space heating control
papers.abstract: Conventional space heating systems typically rely on single or sparse fixed-point temperature measurements, overlooking non-uniform indoor temperature distributions, transient thermal dynamics, and occupant-specific comfort requirements. This study explores an occupant-centric control strategy that aims to maintain the desired temperature around the occupant location. Spatially and temporally varying temperature fields, together with occupant mobility, make real-time local temperature estimation challenging. To address this challenge, we propose a control-oriented Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) model for indoor temperature-field prediction. Conventional PINNs rely on explicit time inputs and assume consistent temporal patterns across samples, which limits adaptability under variable initial conditions and heating sequences. The proposed model infers temporal dynamics implicitly from spatial coordinates and limited sensor measurements, improving robustness to changes in initial conditions and external disturbances. The method was validated across nine horizontal sensing planes in three controlled room-scale configurations. Against a validated COMSOL Multiphysics simulation, the PINN predicted the evaluated temperature fields with a maximum relative error below 1.85% across validation cases. These predictions supported an occupant-centric space heating control scheme. Compared with COMSOL-based offline control, the PINN-based system achieved an average prediction error of around 0.67%, and its rapid inference supports real-time occupant-centric control implementation. This work represents a move away from reliance on fixed-point temperature measurements in space heating control to an occupant-centric control strategy informed by real-time environmental feedback.

papers.title: Xiaomi Auto World Model 2.0: Causal World Models for Real-World Driving and Embodied Intelligence
papers.abstract: We present Xiaomi Auto World Model 2.0, a unified streaming causal world model for Physical AI. It models and generates causal physical evolution in the real world, and unifies heterogeneous conditioning inputs for view-consistent generation. The architecture integrates View-Temporal Attention (VTA) to capture cross-view spatial dependencies and temporal dynamics, together with Multi-view Rotary Position Encoding (RoPE) to encode positional relationships across views and time. WorldRec 2.0 reconstructs static and dynamic 3D Gaussians from multi-view, multi-temporal observations in a single forward pass and uses their renderings as explicit scene context to preserve geometry and appearance during long-horizon generation. Conditioning inputs are fused through VAE latent concatenation in a shared representation space. We incorporate Gated Linear Attention (GLA) into the temporal layers of VTA for efficient streaming inference, reducing computation and KV-cache memory during multi-view rollouts. A physical-interaction data pipeline covers diverse interactions and long-tailed events. From Pre-train onward, these data are combined with large-scale videos and heterogeneous visual modalities to learn visual, geometric, and dynamic priors. During Mid-train, training across diverse view configurations further improves the model's ability to capture how actions and object states shape subsequent scene evolution. After distillation-based Post-train, we apply the model to closed-loop simulation, closed-loop training, and World Action Model (WAM) applications. These applications generate physically consistent future states and support world-state prediction, policy learning, and action generation for Physical AI.

papers.title: OCP-Based Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Quadrotor Trajectory Tracking
papers.abstract: Fast online optimization is essential for nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) on resource-limited aerial platforms. This paper presents an analytical-derivative NMPC solver for quadrotor trajectory tracking. For the state-affine translational model with held thrust and attitude commands, fourth-order Runge--Kutta integration yields an exact discrete-time prediction map. Forward--backward difference equations provide the gradient and exact Hessian of the finite-horizon cost condensed over the input sequence. These derivatives drive a nested optimal-control-based direction recursion, while a shifted warm start reuses the preceding solution. The resulting solver addresses the unconstrained tracking problem without a general-purpose nonlinear programming package. Gazebo experiments show comparable tracking accuracy to iLQR and two acados SQP configurations, with mean solver-time speedups of $1.97$--$2.30$. In onboard flight tests, the mean solver time is $0.3121$\,ms, corresponding to speedups of $3.37$--$5.77$ over the same baselines. The largest measured solver time is $3.7754$\,ms within a $20$-ms control period. These measurements cover the numerical solver and exclude estimation, communication, and command publication.

papers.title: SCOUT: Planning under Occlusion via Object-Centric World Model Rollouts
papers.abstract: Robots manipulating in cluttered spaces must often plan from partial views where foreground objects occlude the target, surrounding geometry, and usable free space. Reactive policies often miss these hidden constraints, while exhaustive search becomes computationally prohibitive in dense clutter. We present SCOUT, an occlusion-aware planning framework that bridges high-level deliberation with grounded physical rollouts. SCOUT leverages an object-centric scene representation to reconstruct hidden geometry and derive a relational planning state capturing blocker hierarchies and accessibility corridors. To navigate the vast action space in clutter, an LLM proposes structured action candidates which are then rigorously evaluated via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) using a learned action-conditioned world model. Evaluations on 'Reveal' and 'Placement' tasks show that SCOUT outperforms Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, embodied agents, and 3D world models, with significant gains in long-horizon tasks requiring reasoning over occluded geometry. We further validate the framework's robustness through real-world robotic manipulation in a cluttered shelf environment.
