papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Joint Generative Modeling of Fault Event Sequences and Sensor Time Series in Solar PV Plants
papers.abstract: This paper presents a multimodal generative model designed to simulate a solar energy plant system for predictive maintenance and fault prediction. We propose a novel approach to enhance system generation through conditional generation by leveraging both event sequences and time-series data and improve next event prediction. The framework employs a Transformer Hawkes Process (THP) to encode event data and an iTransformer to encode time-series data, integrated via a co-attention mechanism that effectively captures cross-modal dependencies between discrete events and continuous signals. From these integrated representations, we employ two specialized decoders for simulation: a Conditional Latent Diffusion Model (CLDM) for modeling future sensor trajectories and the Score Matching-based UnceRtainty quantiFication for Transformer Hawkes Process (SMURF-THP) for high-fidelity event prediction. This dual-decoder strategy supports uncertainty-aware, history-conditioned simulation by rolling the model forward for a specified number of generation iterations, producing finite stochastic scenarios rather than deterministic extrapolations over the full observational record. Evaluated on a comprehensive dataset from the Red Rock Solar Site in Arizona, our approach improves aggregate event-prediction F1 relative to baselines and supports applications in predictive maintenance, fault detection, and energy optimization for solar power systems.

papers.title: Lymphedema as a Significant Risk Factor for Primary Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty Failure: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Total hip and knee arthroplasty are highly effective for improving quality of life, alleviating pain, and enhancing physical function. However, failure of these joint replacements inflicts considerable burdens on patients and the healthcare system. The impact of lymphedema, as an uncommon comorbidity, in patients undergoing total hip and knee arthroplasties remains unknown. This study aimed to assess the most recent publications and evaluate the results and post-operative complications of total joint arthroplasty in patients with preoperative lymphedema. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Embase databases was conducted up to 25th October 2024 to identify relevant studies. Inclusion of studies was established through the application of a predetermined protocol by three independent reviewers. Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal checklists were used for risk of bias assessment. RESULTS: Seven articles met the inclusion criteria. Five studies evaluated the outcomes of lymphedema in total knee arthroplasty, one in total hip arthroplasty, and one in total hip and knee arthroplasty. Lymphedema is a significant risk factor for postoperative complications in total hip and knee arthroplasty. The findings highlight the significance of patient optimization and enable improved lymphedema patient counseling. CONCLUSION: Although lymphedema can be measured as a significant risk factor for complications in total hip and knee arthroplasty, further studies are required to investigate and confirm this relationship.

Interface continuity conditions are imposed to ensure physical consistency between adjacent subdomains. Numerical results show that the proposed method can recover the main features of the piecewise heat-flux profiles and identify the local propagation speeds with relative errors within approximately 5 %. The method provides a flexible framework for describing locally non-uniform moving thermal inputs.

papers.abstract: Ti-6Al-4V lattice structures fabricated by powder bed fusion exhibit compressive responses governed by topology and process-induced material state. This study compares Auxetic, Dode-thin, and Tesseract lattices manufactured by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) and electron beam powder bed fusion (EBPBF). Surface roughness was measured by confocal laser scanning microscopy, microstructure and texture by OM/EBSD, and compression behavior by quasi-static testing and finite element models (FEM), including strut models with measured surfaces. EBPBF struts were rougher than LPBF struts, with R a values of 35.54 and 15.48 μm, respectively. LPBF showed fine acicular α′-like laths, whereas EBPBF showed coarser α+β-like lamellar colonies. LPBF exhibited higher first local peak stresses, particularly for Auxetic and Tesseract, with LPBF Tesseract reaching 229 MPa. Initial collapse resistance did not directly determine energy absorption. LPBF Dode-thin achieved the highest nominal specific energy absorption (SEA) of 6.94 J g −1 at its individual energy-efficiency-based strain limit, whereas LPBF Tesseract had the highest nominal SEA (3.35 J g −1 ) at a common 15% strain. Nominal-geometry lattice FEM overestimated experimental first peak loads by factors of 1.43–2.03. Scaling by a load-bearing diameter d − R z reduced FE/test first-peak ratios to 1.04–1.10 for five of six lattices. Measured EBPBF strut surfaces reduced peak bending moments by 6.6–10.5%, compared with 1.6–3.5% for LPBF surfaces. These results indicate that topology, material state, and surface condition jointly influence lattice compression.

papers.title: Invariant Image Reparameterisation: Bridging Symbolic and Numerical Methods for Identifiability Analysis, Model Reduction, and Prediction
papers.abstract: Structural and practical parameter non-identifiability issues are common when mathematical models are used to interpret data. Such issues motivate model reparameterisation and reduction methods. Here, we consider Invariant Image Reparameterisation (IIR), which asks when symbolic reparameterisation conditions can be replaced by numerical derivative calculations at a single reference point. The central object is the invariant image: a reduced, basis-independent representation of the parameter combinations controlling observable model behaviour. We show that when a one-to-one componentwise transformation makes observable behaviour depend only on fixed linear combinations of the transformed parameters, a single numerical Jacobian determines the associated lower-dimensional reparameterisation space. This includes models depending on monomial combinations of the original parameters. We also give a first-order invariance condition that can rule out a minimal reduction of this form and extracts candidate invariant null directions for an exact non-minimal reduction. In structurally identifiable but practically weakly informed settings, the same calculations separate strongly and weakly informed parameter combinations. The invariant image admits multiple coordinate representations: the SVD gives a default orthonormal basis ordered by local identifiability, while sparse monomial bases are often more interpretable. Treating these coordinates as interest parameters in Profile-Wise Analysis gives likelihood-based uncertainty quantification and prediction. We demonstrate the method on parameterised normal models with Poisson-limit, extended Poisson-limit, and non-limit cases, and on the repressilator, a nonlinear differential equation model of gene regulation. A Julia implementation of IIR, with these and further examples, is available at https://github.com/omaclaren/reparam .

papers.title: Bayesian optimization alleviates the conformational bottleneck in mechanistic modeling
papers.abstract: Thorough treatment of conformation in computational chemistry is required to capture the subtle energy differences that lead to experimental observations. Accurate quantum chemistry calculations are very expensive and evaluation of the entire ensemble found during a conformational search is often unachievable. This is especially true for complex transition state structures such as those in asymmetric catalysis. We develop a Bayesian optimization method to locate the minimum energy conformer of a chemical system, which greatly reduces the numbers of structures that must be optimized with expensive methods, such as DFT. Out of the tens or hundreds of conformers found (up to 625) for each chemical system, we find that our approach required optimization of on average approximately 15% of each system's total search space. Our method finds the lowest energy conformers of flexible transition states in asymmetric catalysis just as rapidly as for single molecules, indicating good general performance even in highly complex cases that are important to real-world chemistry.

papers.title: Effect of Group Size and Resource Constraints on PBL, TBL, and CBL in Healthcare Education: A Scoping Review
papers.abstract: Introduction Active learning pedagogies used in healthcare professional education include Problem-Based Learning (PBL), Case-Based Learning (CBL), and Team-Based Learning (TBL). However, resource constraints and financial pressures have led many institutions to modify these approaches, most commonly by increasing group size. This scoping review aimed to examine how group size influences student learning outcomes. Methods We conducted a scoping review adhering to PRISMA-ScR guidelines, examining studies that examined accredited health professional education programs that compared at least two group sizes and reported on at least one learning outcome. Results Sixteen studies published between 2000 and 2025 met inclusion criteria. Both students and facilitators consistently preferred smaller groups, citing improved engagement, participation, and feedback. Evidence on academic performance was inconclusive, although extremely small groups sometimes performed worse than medium-sized groups. Larger groups were associated with decreased group cohesion and increased subgroup formation. Outside of changes to group size, programs also implemented adaptations such as transitioning from PBL to TBL, modifying facilitation strategies, and altering tutor roles to manage resource constraints. Discussion Smaller group sizes are associated with more positive learner and facilitator experiences and may therefore better support collaborative learning processes. Further research is needed to evaluate the long-term educational and professional impacts of group size and alternative strategies for addressing resource constraints in health professional education.

papers.title: CHEMICAL-TECHNOLOGICAL PRECONDITIONS FOR DIGITAL TWIN IMPLEMENTATION IN POLYMER PROCESSING: A DOCUMENTED TECHNOLOGY BASELINE FROM BULGARIAN PLASTICS
papers.abstract: Digital Twin technology is increasingly proposed for polymer processing, yet the chemical-technological conditions that make a twin useful, and the equipment baseline required to build one, are rarely examined together against documented industrial evidence. This paper establishes why polymer processing is a favourable domain for Digital Twin implementation and then tests how far the necessary preconditions are met in a national producing sector. The argument proceeds from polymer physics. Because melt viscosity is strongly shear- and temperature-dependent, and because thermal history governs crystallization, shrinkage and residual stress, a fixed set of machine settings does not reproduce a fixed process state when polymer grade, recycled fraction, moisture content or additive level varies. A twin is valuable in this domain precisely because the state variables that determine part quality cannot be measured directly in production. Against this background, a technology inventory was compiled for a census of 29 Bulgarian plastics manufacturers (NACE 22.2x), of which 20 firms have documented process-level evidence. Extrusion is documented at 13 of the 20 firms, injection moulding at 5 and internal recycling at 4, with thermoforming, coating and blow moulding at 1 - 2 firms each; 7 of the 20 firms disclose named equipment. Sensor-level process instrumentation is documented at no firm, and no firm provides evidence of an ERP, MES or SCADA system, or of a Digital Twin. On the classification applied here, no firm falls in the confirmed Digital Twin category and three fall in the Digital-Twin-ready category. The binding constraint in this sector is therefore not modelling capability but the absenceof the in-process measurements – melt temperature, melt pressure, cavity pressure and screw torque - from which any twin state estimate must be constructed. Firms processing recycled feedstock have the strongest technological case for instrumenting first.

papers.abstract: Distributed drive electric vehicles face vibration and noise challenges due to the coupling of high-frequency electromagnetic excitation, time-varying meshing stiffness, and thermal deformation, forming a typical electromechanical-thermal multi-field coupled vibration. A systematic investigation into this coupling mechanism and suppression strategy is presented. An electromechanical-thermal multi-field dynamic model is established to reveal multi-field interactions. A hierarchical collaborative suppression method is proposed: structural optimization reduces transmission vibration; control-level model predictive control with harmonic current injection mitigates electromagnetic excitation; thermal-level coolant regulation suppresses thermally induced vibration. Dynamometer tests show that the proposed method reduces critical component vibration by 5 dB(A), significantly improving NVH performance. This study offers a complete technical pathway for low-noise design from mechanism analysis to suppression implementation.

papers.title: Flow dynamics mechanisms and thermal hydraulic performance evaluation of triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) heat exchangers
papers.abstract: Heat exchangers (HX) based on triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures provide new opportunities for manipulating internal flow organization and enhancing thermal transport. This study systematically compares the thermohydraulic performance of five representative TPMS HX, including Primitive, I-graph Wrapped Package (IWP), Gyroid, Diamond, and F-Rhombic Dodecahedron (FRD), against a conventional Printed Circuit Heat Exchanger (PCHE) under identical geometric dimensions with 70% porosity. Computational fluid dynamics simulations are performed over a Reynolds number (Re) range of 500–3000 and validated experimentally using additively manufactured prototypes. The results reveal that the continuous three-dimensional curvatures and interconnected pathways of TPMS structures fundamentally alter flow organization by inducing secondary flows, transverse mixing, and thermal boundary layer redevelopment. Different topologies achieve heat transfer enhancement through distinct mechanisms: Gyroid and Diamond promote helical secondary flows through curvature variation, while FRD strengthens flow disturbance through periodic contraction and redirection. Consequently, all TPMS HX exhibit superior heat transfer performance compared with the PCHE. At Re = 500, the FRD HX increases the total heat transfer rate and overall heat transfer coefficient by 69% and 78%, respectively. However, enhanced heat transfer is accompanied by increased hydraulic resistance, with normalized pressure drops ranging from 8.6 Pa/W for IWP to 34.3 Pa/W for FRD. The Gyroid and Diamond HX achieve a favorable balance between flow-induced enhancement and hydraulic penalty. These findings clarify the topology-flow-thermal relationship of TPMS HX and provide physical guidance for the design of compact liquid-cooling systems, particularly for applications such as electronic cooling and battery thermal management.

papers.title: Meaningful Learning, Bloom’s Taxonomy, Active Learning Methodologies, and the Flipped Classroom: Theoretical Contributions to Library and Information Science Education
papers.abstract: As transformações ocorridas no ensino superior e as demandas contemporâneas da formação profissional têm ampliado o debate sobre abordagens pedagógicas capazes de promover processos de aprendizagem mais participativos, reflexivos e significativos. No contexto da Biblioteconomia, essas discussões assumem especial relevância diante da necessidade de formar profissionais aptos a atuar em ambientes informacionais cada vez mais complexos e dinâmicos. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar comparativamente a Aprendizagem Significativa, a Taxonomia de Bloom, as Metodologias Ativas e a Sala de Aula Invertida, identificando suas principais características, convergências, distinções e possibilidades de articulação para o ensino superior em Biblioteconomia. Trata-se de uma pesquisa qualitativa, de caráter descritivo-comparativo de abordagem teórico-conceitual, desenvolvida por meio de revisão integrativa da literatura. Os resultados indicam que, embora possuam naturezas e funções distintas no processo educacional, as perspectivas analisadas apresentam convergências relacionadas à participação do estudante, à autonomia na aprendizagem, à valorização de processos cognitivos mais complexos e à articulação entre teoria e prática. A comparação realizada também permitiu identificar possibilidades de articulação entre essas perspectivas, evidenciando seu potencial para subsidiar reflexões sobre práticas pedagógicas voltadas à formação bibliotecária. Conclui-se que a análise comparativa dessas abordagens oferece contribuições teóricas para a discussão de alternativas metodológicas alinhadas aos desafios contemporâneos da formação em Biblioteconomia.

papers.title: Hybrid ML-Weibull Predictive Maintenance System for Dynamic Tire Remaining Useful Life Estimation
papers.abstract: Tire failure is a major contributor to road fatalities, accounting for 3-15 of fatal accidents globally. Conventional Tire Pressure Monitoring Systems (TPMS) are limited by their reactive nature, as they only alert drivers to under-inflation after it occurs and cannot predict gradual wear or Remaining Useful Life (RUL). This research proposes a hybrid Predictive Maintenance framework that integrates Machine Learning with the Weibull reliability distribution to provide dynamic RUL estimations. Unlike existing simulation-centric or static models, the developed system utilizes an edge-cloud architecture centered on an ESP32-S3 gateway to capture telemetry from TPMS, OBD-II, and GPS modules. By treating the Weibull scale parameter (λ) as a dynamic covariate influenced by operational stressors such as engine load, vehicle speed, pressure, and temperature, the model continuously adapts to the tire’s degradation trajectory. Empirical results from field testing demonstrate that the covariate-driven approach significantly outperforms static baselines. The LightGBM regressor achieved the highest precision with a near-negligible MAPE of 0.0025 and a MASE of 0.2168. Specialized reliability metrics, including MQWE, further confirm the model's ability to minimize high-risk outliers, while an analysis of pessimistic error profiles ensures that maintenance is prompted before catastrophic failure. This study provides a scalable, real-time solution for in-vehicle Prognostics and Health Management (PHM), offering a robust pathway to reducing tire-related road casualties.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables complex 316 L stainless‐steel food‐processing components, but surface finishing affects both cleanability and corrosion. Wrought (WR), as‐built (AB), mechanically polished (MP), and electropolished (EP) surfaces were compared using topography, wettability, whey‐protein fouling and alkaline cleaning, hygienic endpoints, and polarization in 3.5 wt% NaCl. AB had the largest valley volume and developed area, retained the most protein after cleaning, and had the highest corrosion current density. Cleaning efficiency ranked MP (97.3%) > WR (95.5%) > EP (94.7%) > AB (91.4%). EP had the lowest corrosion current density (0.190 ± 0.020 μA cm −2 ) and highest operational breakdown potential (0.483 ± 0.012 V vs. SCE), whereas WR had a lower breakdown potential than AB. Thus, defect‐rich surfaces can impair both functions, but the cleanability and electrochemical optima differ. LPBF food‐contact surfaces require joint qualification, with corrosion metrics providing complementary surface‐state information rather than stand‐alone prediction of cleaning efficiency.

papers.title: Fdm-based 4D printed polymer blends: characteristics and applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Shape memory polymers are a distinct category of intelligent materials that can change their configuration in response to external stimuli, such as moisture, light, or temperature. 4-dimensional (4D) printing offers the advantages of 3-dimensional printing and shape-memory capability. The use of polymer blends offers an effective strategy to enhance the overall shape memory effect, including improvements in shape recovery, shape fixity, response time, and recovery speed, while simultaneously tailoring mechanical performance. This review presents a comprehensive overview of material selection, blend composition, and relationships between structure, properties, and stimuli in fused deposition modeling (FDM)-based 4D-printed polymer blends. The key characterization techniques used to assess thermal, mechanical, and shape-memory behaviors are critically discussed. Recent advances in polymer blend systems, including PLA, PETG, TPU, PCL, and ABS-based blends, are reviewed. Further, their emerging applications in biomedical devices, soft robotics, aerospace, and smart structures are discussed. Finally, the current challenges in printability, interfacial compatibility, rheology, and reproducibility, along with future research directions, are outlined to advance FDM-based 4D printed polymer blend systems.

papers.title: AlMg transmission measurements on the National Ignition Facility with novel uncertainty quantification method for point-projection geometry
papers.abstract: The opacity platform on the National Ignition Facility (NIF) was developed to study the opacities of important elements in the solar mixture such as Fe and O as well as mid- to high-Z elements. The platform is intended to help address the discrepancy between measured vs calculated opacities first demonstrated in experiments at the Sandia National Laboratories Z-machine. This discrepancy lies at the heart of the solar problem: the fact that helioseismic measurements disagree with stellar structure models, which depend sensitively on calculated opacities. If correct, the opacity measured on Z would substantially reduce the disagreement. An independent platform has been developed at the National Ignition Facility to verify this result and extend opacity measurements to other elements and plasma conditions. The NIF platform employs different methods from Z. Point-projection absorption spectroscopy provides information about the unattenuated, attenuated, and self-emission signals needed to infer transmission, but the measurement is complicated by non-ideal effects. The work described here is based on the Monte Carlo-based uncertainty analysis pioneered by the Z experimental team. Here, we provide similar methods that introduce the capability of accounting for these effects in point-projection geometry for the first time in a statistically rigorous way. The uncertainty analysis method presented here requires dedicated calibration datasets. Enough dedicated calibration datasets have been obtained to enable development of the framework. Additional data will need to be obtained to refine the uncertainty analysis. We apply the method to transmission spectra from Al:Mg plasmas in the ∼1100–1800 eV photon energy range collected using an elliptical crystal spectrometer in a spatially resolving, point-projection geometry.

papers.abstract: Although numerous polymer and ceramic coatings have been developed for metal implants, achieving long-term corrosion protection while maintaining favorable immune responses remains a significant challenge. This study developed and evaluated multifunctional hybrid nylon (PA)/chitosan (CS)/hydroxyapatite (HAp)/TiO₂ biocoatings deposited on 316 L stainless steel (316 L SS) by dip-coating to improve corrosion resistance and biological performance for implant applications. Two formulations, PA84%/CS10%/HAp5%/TiO₂1% and PA89%/CS5%/HAp5%/TiO₂1%, were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), mechanical testing, cell viability assays with RAW-Blue macrophages, NF-κB activation analysis, and electrochemical evaluation in Hank's solution for 120 days. The coatings exhibited homogeneous porous morphologies, indicating integration between the polymeric matrix and ceramic phases. This microstructure was accompanied by cell viability approaching 98%, while NF-κB activation remained low compared with the inflammatory control, demonstrating a cellular response compatible with biomedical applications. Although CS, HAp, and TiO₂ incorporation reduced the mechanical performance relative to neat PA, the hybrid biocoatings retained ductility and resilience suitable for flexible coating applications, with PA84%/CS10%/HAp5%/TiO₂1% showing the best balance among the composites. Electrochemical tests demonstrated enhanced corrosion protection compared with uncoated 316 L SS. Among the evaluated systems, PA84%/CS10%/HAp5%/TiO₂1% showed the best performance, exhibiting the lowest corrosion current density (3.00E-07 mA/cm 2 ) and the highest impedance modulus (90372 Ω.cm 2 ) after 120 days of immersion. This behavior was attributed to the multifunctional protective layer, which combines barrier effect, interfacial stability, and diffusion-controlled ionic transport, due to the coating-passive layer synergy. These results indicate the potential of PA/CS/HAp/TiO₂ biocoatings to enhance long-term corrosion protection and biologically compatible surfaces for metallic implants.

papers.title: Active Symmetry Support Control for Grid-Following/Grid-Forming Hybrid Renewable Energy Stations Considering Transient Synchronization Stability
papers.abstract: An active symmetry support control method based on model predictive control and incorporating transient synchronization security boundaries is developed for a grid-following (GFL)/grid-gorming (GFM) hybrid renewable-energy station comprising GFL wind energy and GFM energy storage. The control objective is to suppress disturbance-induced departures from the dynamic balance between generation-side support and grid/load demand, which are referred to here as power asymmetry rather than phase-domain three-phase imbalance, and to restore a power-symmetric operating state through coordinated active- and reactive-power support. Reduced-order transient synchronization models are established separately for the GFL phase-locked loop and the GFM virtual synchronous generator without explicitly constructing a transient coupling model between the two converter types. For the GFM converter, damping energy is incorporated into the fault-stage transient-energy balance. The resulting transient-energy functions and critical-energy criteria are used to determine the synchronization-stability boundaries, which are then mapped into dynamically updated P-Q feasible regions. A frequency–voltage prediction model combining a system frequency-response model and a point-of-common-coupling voltage-sensitivity model is then established. The GFL/GFM transient-energy constraints, dynamic P-Q security regions, power-regulation capability limits, and command-direction constraints are embedded in the receding-horizon optimization to coordinate active- and reactive-power support while preserving transient synchronization security. Local linearization of the transient-energy constraints and second-order-cone reformulation of the dynamic P-Q regions are adopted to improve online computational efficiency. papers.title: Gelatin–itaconate enables room-temperature extrusion-based 3D printing as a high-performance, sustainable alternative to GelMA
papers.abstract: Gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) is a widely used photocrosslinkable biomaterial for tissue engineering and biofabrication; however, its synthesis relies on petroleum-derived methacrylic anhydride/acid, and its precursor formulations generally require low-temperature processing to achieve sufficient printability. Here, we present gelatin–itaconate (GelIA), synthesized using bio-based itaconic acid, as a sustainable alternative to GelMA for room-temperature extrusion-based 3D printing. To isolate the influence of functional-group chemistry, GelIA and GelMA were synthesized with equivalent degrees of functionalization (36–38%) and systematically characterized by TNBS assay, ¹H NMR, FTIR, SEM, rheology, in situ photorheology, compression testing, swelling, enzymatic degradation, tissue adhesion, and printability evaluation. Compared with GelMA, GelIA exhibited higher precursor viscosity, pronounced shear-thinning behavior, improved structural recovery, and enabled stable extrusion-based 3D printing at 21–23 °C using only 5% (w/v) polymer, whereas GelMA with the same degree of functionalization was not printable under identical conditions. Following photocrosslinking, GelIA formed a more interconnected hydrogel network with enhanced viscoelastic properties, higher effective crosslink density, improved compressive properties, superior tissue adhesion, and greater structural integrity, resulting in enhanced stress-relaxation behavior. Despite exhibiting a higher swelling capacity, GelIA degraded more slowly than GelMA, indicating improved hydrogel stability. These findings validate our hypothesis that the additional carboxylic acid functionality of bio-based itaconate strengthens intermolecular interactions within the gelatin network, thereby improving both precursor rheology and hydrogel performance without increasing polymer concentration. Collectively, GelIA represents not only a sustainable, high-performance alternative to GelMA but also demonstrates how rational functional-group engineering can be exploited to regulate intermolecular interactions, enabling next-generation photocrosslinkable bioinks for room-temperature biofabrication and tissue engineering.

papers.title: Computational Models of the Foreign Body Response: A Focus on Biomaterial Properties
papers.abstract: The foreign body response (FBR) is the main biological process governing the long-term performance and safety of implantable biomaterials. As the FBR is complex, multifactorial, and unfolds over extended time scales, making in vitro replication challenging, standard biological evaluation frameworks continue to rely primarily on in vivo testing In this context, computational modeling offers a promising strategy to improve the fundamental understanding of FBR mechanisms, support biomaterial design, and reduce dependency on animal experimentation. Existing approaches, including ordinary differential equation (ODE), partial differential equation (PDE), and agent-based (AB) models, have provided important insights into inflammatory signaling, macrophage dynamics, fibrosis progression, and capsule formation. However, most computational models still treat the FBR in a simplified way and rarely integrate material-dependent effects in a quantitative manner, despite the well-established role of surface chemistry, topography, stiffness, and other properties in shaping host responses. This review summarizes the current state of the art in computational models of the FBR, including both mechanistic and data-driven methods, with a particular focus on how material properties are represented. We discuss the main limitations of current modeling approaches as well as the scarcity of standardized experimental data suitable for calibration and validation, and highlight the need for closer interplay between hybrid predictive models and experimental data, with a digital twin (DT) of the FBR representing the ultimate objective of these efforts.

papers.title: Digital twin-based online forging stress prediction for fast forging hydraulic presses
papers.abstract: In fast forging hydraulic presses, the equivalent internal stress of forgings directly determines the forming quality and the service life of the resulting components. However, such stress cannot be directly measured during forging operations, which limits real-time process monitoring and quality control. To address this challenge, a digital twin-driven method is proposed to rapidly predict the equivalent stress of forgings. A multi-domain digital twin model is constructed by integrating a hydraulic model of the fast forging press with a finite element (FE) model of the workpiece. Equivalent stress data corresponding to various operating conditions are systematically generated through FE simulation, thereby providing the training dataset for surrogate modeling. On this basis, an adaptively fused LSTM-XGBoost surrogate model is developed. MC Dropout and ensemble learning strategies are employed to quantify the uncertainty of the LSTM and XGBoost sub-models, respectively. The results indicate that the proposed adaptive LSTM-XGBoost surrogate model achieves a coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) of 0.971 and a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 12.3 MPa. To enable online equivalent stress prediction, the trained surrogate is coupled with a Simulink-based hydraulic model that reproduces the real-world operating behavior of the fast forging hydraulic press. This configuration enables online stress prediction driven by real-time process parameters generated by the hydraulic simulation model. The proposed method offers a simulation-based approach to online stress prediction for forging operations, providing a foundation for future physical deployment. It also provides guidance for improving the forming quality of large-scale forgings and optimizing relevant process parameters.

papers.abstract: Accurate modeling of Short Fiber Reinforced Composites (SFRCs) remains computationally expensive for full-field simulations. Data-driven surrogate models using artificial neural networks have been proposed as an efficient alternative to numerical modeling, where Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are increasingly being used for path-dependent multiscale modeling. However, recently, transformer models have been developed and they offer scalability and efficient parallelization, yet have not been systematically compared with RNNs in this field. In this study, we perform a systematic comparison between RNNs and transformer models trained on sequences of homogenized response of SFRC. We study the effect of two types of hyperparameters, namely architectural hyperparameters (such as the number of GRU layers, hidden size, number of attention heads, and encoder blocks) and training hyperparameters (such as learning rate and batch size). Both sets of hyperparameters are tuned using Bayesian optimization. We then analyze scaling laws with respect to dataset size and inference accuracy in interpolation and extrapolation regimes. Results show that while transformer models remain competitive in terms of accuracy on large datasets, the RNNs demonstrate better accuracy on small datasets. Furthermore, under extrapolation, the RNN is more accurate, while the transformer is seven times faster at inference when evaluating complete sequences offline.

In single-solute batch experiments, AC-PDD demonstrated the highest maximum adsorption capacities at equilibrium reaching 586.1 and 445.6 mg g-1 for 2-NP and 4-NP, respectively. Binary-solute adsorption allowed to remove both NPs (total maximum adsorption capacity of 453.8 mg g-1) and revealed antagonistic interaction between them, deeply studied at different NP initial concentrations (20-100 mg L-1). Adsorbents were reused over multiple cycles after regeneration with ethanol and AC-PDD exhibited the highest regeneration efficiency (> 70 %). For continuous-flow assays, monoliths with gyroid lattice structure were synthesized via digital light processing 3D-printing and subsequent carbonization and steam activation, resulting in G-AC-PDD sample. G-AC-PDD monoliths showed broad breakthrough curves with longer saturation times (more than one month) and preferential retention of 2-NP over 4-NP. Dynamic adsorption capacities (356.8 and 260.2 mg g-1 for 2-NP and 4-NP, respectively) exceeded the values obtained in batch mode for binary system at the same inlet concentration and a 0.2 mL min-1 of flowrate. These results demonstrate that carbon monoliths with high uptake capacities may be produced by additive manufacturing for the efficient removal of lipophilic compounds from aqueous solutions.

papers.title: From Point Defect Model to Equivalent Circuit: A Diagnostic Framework for Electrochemical Impedance Analysis of Passive Films
papers.abstract: The Point Defect Model (PDM) is a widely accepted mechanistic framework for describing passive film formation and breakdown on metals, such as titanium. However, its application to experimental systems is often hindered by complex parameter spaces and issues of non-uniqueness in parameter identification. Conventional Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) fitting using empirical equivalent circuits frequently lacks direct physical meaning, further complicating mechanistic interpretation. This study introduces a mathematically rigorous analytical equivalence between the impedance response of the PDM and a physically grounded equivalent circuit model, explicitly deriving relationships between PDM kinetic parameters and circuit elements. Because the resulting circuit can be fitted with commercially available software, the framework allows researchers to test quickly whether their impedance data are consistent with the PDM. A good fit is necessary but not sufficient: the fitted circuit elements must also take values that the PDM allows. We validated this approach using EIS data from Ti-6Al-4V samples, produced via laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M), in both chloride and acidic environments. The impedance of the thin native passive films was well described by the derived circuit, whereas that of a film anodized at 30 V and measured at the open circuit potential, i.e. far from the steady state assumed by the PDM, was not; the framework thus correctly identified this film as lying outside the regime in which the PDM assumptions hold. The native films, however, showed a faradaic capacitance more than two orders of magnitude below the value that the PDM requires for the relaxation of the film thickness. Although the transformation relates each circuit element to PDM quantities, it does not remove the non-uniqueness of the individual kinetic parameters; its main value lies in diagnosing whether the PDM is applicable to a given system.

papers.title: Design of patient-specific metamaterial orthopedic implants enabled by field-driven lattice grading for additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: Stress shielding caused by stiffness mismatch between metallic femoral stems and bone contributes to bone resorption and implant loosening after total hip arthroplasty. This study presents a patient-specific computational framework integrating topology optimization (TO), continuous field-driven lattice grading, automated design exploration, and biomechanical evaluation. A Ti-6Al-4V stem was optimized under peak static physiological loading to generate a spatial density field, which was continuously mapped to architecture-specific geometric parameters. The same TO-derived field was used as a common mechanical control field for three distinct architectures: strut-based Diamond, TPMS-based Gyroid, and stochastic Voronoi, under identical anatomical and loading conditions. A Python-based constrained full-factorial design-of-experiments workflow explored architecture-specific parameters against a common intact-femur stiffness target, enabling controlled comparison of how different lattice representations realize the same patient-specific optimization objective. The optimized stems achieved 53–57% porosity, intact-femur-like deformation, pore sizes predominantly within 500–1050 μm, and surface-to-volume ratios of 2.011–3.45 mm −1 . Compared with the solid stem, graded architectures reduced stiffness by 41–49% and Gruen-zone stress shielding from 55 to 75% to 18–36%, while maintaining stresses below the Ti-6Al-4V yield strength. The framework enables systematic architecture-dependent design and biomechanical evaluation of patient-specific graded porous implants.

papers.title: A Systematic Review of Battery Digital Twins for Thermal Safety, State Estimation, and Remaining Useful Life Prediction towards Predictive Maintenance
papers.abstract: Cyber-physical systems in the e-transportation era have emerged as an advancement in the Electric Vehicle (EV) industry. Batteries are a prominent research product of EVs, driving progress towards the saturation of Industrial Revolution 5.0 by enhancing their efficiency, performance, and safety criteria. The current study provides a detailed survey on the implementation of Digital Twin Technology (DTT), a cyber-physical system in EV batteries. Battery Digital Twins (BDTs), which couple a physical battery with a continuously updated virtual counterpart, are widely proposed for this purpose; however, existing reviews rarely evaluates the level of BDT. This review addresses one central question: the extension of BDT implementations that satisfy the defining requirements of a digital twin while delivering the three functions on which predictive maintenance depends, namely thermal safety, state estimation and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction. The review contributes an operational BDT definition and maturity classification, a reproducible evidence base and a research agenda prioritizing field-data validation, uncertainty-aware RUL prediction, bidirectional synchronization, interoperability and cybersecurity, with implications for researchers, battery manufacturers, fleet operators and digital-twin developers, thereby contributing to Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG-7).

papers.title: Engineering Microstructural Heterogeneity for Enhanced Machinability of Additive Manufactured Inconel 718 superalloys
papers.abstract: Powder bed fusion (PBF) technology has enabled the fabrication of high-performance nickel-based superalloys, yet the influence of process-induced microstructural heterogeneity on their machinability remains unexplored. Herein, we demonstrate the relationship between additive manufacturing (AM) process, microstructural evolution, machinability and surface integrity of Inconel 718 (IN718) fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM) and electron beam melting (EBM), PBF technologies. SLM produced a refined cellular-dendritic microstructure with interdendritic Laves-phase segregation and relatively weak crystallographic texture, achieving high strength and ductility. Conversely, EBM promotes equiaxed grains with pronounced crystallographic texture and secondary phases features, resulting in higher hardness (∼ 410 HV) but lower tensile strength and ductility. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) revealed elongated, faceted nanoscale precipitates and lamellar features that further revealed distinct nanoscale precipitate morphologies and lamellar features, endowing the influence of the process conditions on microstructural evolution. These contrasting microstructures led to markedly different responses during face milling. Notably, SLM- IN718 exhibited lower cutting forces and a better surface finish (Ra = 0.1–0.3 μm), whereas EBM-printed IN718 showed higher cutting forces and surface roughness (Ra = 0.1–0.4 μm), accompanied by localized material pull-out and surface tearing. Fractographic observations further revealed distinct ductile dimple formation in SLM specimens from dendrite-associated fracture features in EBM specimens. The dominant mechanical response reflects a strength–hardness trade-off: the SLM-IN718 with high strength and ductility (UTS ≈ 1010 MPa; YS ≈ 834 MPa). Our findings provide multiscale insight into the direct mechanistic link between PBF-induced microstructural heterogeneity and post-fabrication machinability, revealing how nanoscale substructures, phase distribution and mechanical response govern the machinability of additively manufactured IN718.

papers.title: Strengthening mechanism of interpenetrating lattice structures in removal-free capsules fabricated by laser powder bed fusion for hot isostatic pressing
papers.abstract: Removal-free capsules made of the same material as the encapsulated powder avoid contamination caused by elemental diffusion during hot isostatic pressing (HIP). However, the planar bonding interface between the consolidated powder matrix and the HIP-processed capsule in the Powder-Capsule specimen is prone to interfacial defects and stress concentration, ultimately leading to interfacial failure. In this work, GH3536 conformal removal-free capsules with Gyroid lattice structures were fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), filled with GH3536 powder, and consolidated by HIP to form a bicontinuous interpenetrating structure. The effects of Gyroid unit cell size and volume fraction on interfacial microstructures and tensile properties were investigated. The C8-V30 specimen, featuring a Gyroid lattice structure with an 8 mm unit cell size and volume fraction of 30%, exhibited the best mechanical performance among the investigated Gyroid lattice structures, achieving an ultimate tensile strength of 692.5 MPa and an elongation at break of 22.5%, representing increases of 22.1% and 125.0%, respectively, compared with the Powder-Capsule specimen. The C8-V30 specimen exhibited fewer visible interfacial defects in the examined regions, suggesting improved interfacial integrity. Furthermore, finite element analysis revealed load redistribution and coordinated plastic deformation within the interpenetrating structure. The modified rule of mixtures predicted 616.0 MPa for C8-V30, indicating a 76.5 MPa strength difference potentially associated in part with mechanical interlocking within the bicontinuous interpenetrating structure. The findings elucidate the strengthening mechanism of the bicontinuous interpenetrating structure and provide guidance for the design of removal-free capsules.

papers.title: Outcome-Based Education (OBE)-based digital financial learning through the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model
papers.abstract: This study was prompted by the need for students to develop the digital competencies required to meet the challenges of Industry 4.0, particularly in managing finances through digital technology. Outcome-Based Education (OBE) emphasises achieving specified competencies as learning outcomes, whereas the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model encourages students to strengthen their analytical and problem-solving skills and apply digital finance concepts through real-world case studies. Employing a descriptive qualitative design, the study drew on classroom observations, interviews with lecturers and students, and documentation of learning outcomes. The findings indicate that implementing PBL within an OBE framework effectively enhances students' practical skills in using digital finance applications, fosters critical and collaborative thinking, and deepens their understanding of financial concepts. Students demonstrated improved competencies in financial planning, risk analysis, and the use of digital tools for financial management. These results confirm that integrating OBE with PBL provides an effective learning framework for preparing graduates to meet the professional challenges of digital finance. The study recommends developing competency-based curricula that use active learning methods aligned with industry needs.

papers.title: Design, Manufacturing and Applications of Polymer-Based Architected Cellular Materials by Direct Vat Photopolymerization: A Focused Review
papers.abstract: Vat photopolymerization (VPP) enables the fabrication of polymer-based architected cellular materials with fine members, continuous surfaces, and internal geometries that are difficult to realize using many other polymer additive manufacturing processes. This focused narrative review considers directly fabricated, retained-polymer lattices produced by single-photon laser-scanning and projection VPP, including stereolithography (SLA), digital light processing (DLP), masked stereolithography (mSLA/LCD), projection micro-stereolithography (PµSL), and continuous projection variants. A Scopus search yielded a screened journal corpus of 461 articles for descriptive mapping, from which 195 records were selected purposively for detailed synthesis. The literature shows sustained growth in publication volume and broader representation of TPMS, auxetic, graded, hierarchical, biomimetic, non-periodic, composite, and multifunctional concepts. Across application domains, the recurring constraint is the coupling among architecture, photopolymer behavior, and manufacturing accuracy. Feature scale, separation, washing, post-curing, and defects can alter the as-built geometry and its function. Continuous progress will require component-scale validation, reproducibility, standardized reporting, durable materials with demonstrated recovery or end-of-life pathways, and workflows that connect design, process planning, metrology, performance, qualification, and end-of-life considerations.

papers.title: Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Learning-Assisted Horizon Selection for Model Predictive Control of an Experimentally Identified Water Process System
papers.abstract: Model Predictive Control (MPC) performance depends on prediction and control horizons, particularly for experimentally identified inverse-response processes with noise, actuator constraints, and plant–model mismatch. This study evaluates an offline reinforcement learning (RL)-assisted supervisory framework for horizon selection in constrained MPC of a membrane-filtration process. Pump-speed-command and pump-line-flow data identified a second-order state-space model using Numerical Algorithms for Subspace State-Space System Identification (N4SID), achieving 92.16% estimation fit and 90.90% independent one-step-ahead validation fit, although long-horizon fidelity remained limited. The model was embedded in target-tracking MPC with input and input-move constraints, while RL selected only the horizons. Nominally, the representative RL-selected pair reduced the prespecified composite score from 2.5700 to 2.4562 (4.43%) with zero simulated quadratic-programming failures. Exhaustive evaluation of 146 feasible pairs identified 1.2214, confirming that RL was not globally optimal. Under a 120-iteration budget, Bayesian optimisation reached the global optimum in 20/30 runs versus 3/30 for epsilon-greedy. Extending the domain to 208 pairs reduced the score to 1.1838, indicating sensitivity to the lower prediction-horizon bound. Across 11 model-based robustness scenarios, RL-tuned MPC achieved an average 3.13% score reduction versus baseline, with individual-metric trade-offs. Overall, horizon selection improved the MPC trade-off, but results remained dependent on the search domain and identified-model environment.

papers.title: State-Adaptive and Tail-Risk-Aware Rolling Control of Wind–Solar–VRFB Systems with Experimentally Calibrated Power Envelopes
papers.abstract: State-adaptive risk-aware rolling model predictive control (SA-RR-MPC) links experimentally calibrated battery action limits to grid-side tracking and ramp-risk costs in wind–solar–vanadium redox flow battery (VRFB) regulation. Protocol-matched PNNL cycling observations supply power envelopes conditioned on a continuous charge reference and measured capacity, while Mendeley pressure–flow measurements supply the normalized pump-loss shape. Pump-corrected net injection connects admitted stack actions to scenario conditional value at risk (CVaR). A two-pass linear program selects dispatch requests, and current-state projection provides minimum-correction execution with an explicit bound on the resulting ramp-risk perturbation. Whole-cycle calibration checks give 89.95% Q90 coverage, and the local power labels change by at most 0.205% under the common charge-reference comparison. A causal 184-day NSRDB/WIND Toolkit replay evaluates a nominal 20 MW/80 MWh VRFB under common empirical-envelope and energy protection for all storage methods. SA-RR-MPC reduces realized ramp-exceedance CVaR90 by 40.94% and request-to-execution correction energy by 65.64% relative to Fixed-MPC, with a 0.54% increase in tracking RMSE. Relative to a matched risk-aware controller differing only in predictive power bounds, correction energy falls by 58.48%. Two nonoverlapping 28-day weather windows and three paired scenario seeds retain 27.06–50.01% CVaR90 reductions relative to Fixed-MPC. Paired module tests identify complementary roles in request adaptation, net-power prediction, and tail-risk valuation. The 95th-percentile serial software-loop time is 18.54 ms over 624 cycles after 48 warm-up steps.

papers.title: A Composite‐Kernel Mixture of Experts GPR Framework With Bayesian Hyperparameter Optimization for Accurate Mass Prediction in Greenhouse Solar Dryer
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study evaluated Gaussian process regression (GPR) models—Basic GPR, MoE‐GPR, and Bayesian‐optimized MoE‐GPR (BO‐MoE‐GPR)—for predicting product mass during greenhouse solar drying using solar radiation, temperature, and humidity as inputs. Pearson's correlation matrix (PCM) analysis revealed strong positive correlations between radiation and temperature, negative correlations between humidity and radiation, and moderate‐to‐strong negative correlations between environmental inputs and product mass, showing temperature to be the strongest linear correlate of mass loss, while noting that correlation does not establish causal dominance. Among 11 classical regression models, the Exponential model showed the best performance ( R 2 = 0.9936, MAPE = 5.5100%). The BO‐MoE‐GPR achieved superior training accuracy ( R 2 = 0.9996, MAPE = 0.68%) over Basic GPR ( R 2 = 0.9993, MAPE = 1.39%), corresponding to an approximately 51% reduction in training MAPE. Cross‐validation confirmed BO‐MoE‐GPR's robustness ( R 2 = 0.985 ± 0.009, MAPE = 1.07% ± 0.05%) versus Basic GPR ( R 2 = 0.939 ± 0.090, MAPE = 5.24% ± 1.89%), with tighter residual errors (−2% to +2%) and accurate tracking of all drying phases. The composite kernel and MoE framework effectively captured heterogeneous drying patterns, while Bayesian optimization efficiently tuned hyperparameters. The novelty of this work lies in demonstrating that the nonstationary, multiregime nature of greenhouse solar drying data can be explicitly exploited by a GMM‐based mixture of experts GPR architecture with composite RBF + Matérn 3/2 kernels and Bayesian‐optimized hyperparameters, rather than by applying conventional single global GPR models. The framework provides accurate mass predictions from environmental inputs alone and therefore shows promise for future non‐invasive monitoring and model‐based control applications, although these practical benefits remain to be demonstrated experimentally.

papers.title: From alert fatigue to autonomous defense: A systematic literature review of AI-driven SIEM–SOAR integration in security operations centers
papers.abstract: Next-generation Security Operations Centers (SOCs) are increasingly adopting Artificial Intelligence (AI) to address the persistent “detection deficit” and mitigate the problem of alert fatigue associated with traditional signature-based security systems. This Systematic Literature Review (SLR) evaluates the integration of AI-driven Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) and Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) platforms as enablers of proactive cyber defense. Following the three-phase SLR methodology proposed by Kitchenham and Charters, this review analyzes 50 primary studies published between 2015 and 2026, covering data sources that include enterprise logs, Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT), and synthetic benchmarks. The findings reveal a clear shift toward context-aware architectures that leverage MITRE ATT&CK mappings and causal graph analytics to reconstruct multi-stage attack scenarios. Several studies report detection rates exceeding 95% under controlled experimental conditions; however, performance generalization to real-world production environments remains a critical open challenge. Emerging trends highlight Bayesian uncertainty quantification and synthetic data augmentation as promising strategies for addressing the scarcity of labeled real-world security telemetry. Despite these advances, significant research gaps persist, including the limited explainability of deep learning models used in high-stakes decision contexts, insufficient study of the long-term effects of automation on analyst cognitive load, and a lack of rigorous adversarial robustness evaluation. This review concludes by proposing a comprehensive research roadmap for transitioning toward autonomous, human-centered security operations.

papers.title: Predictive Nanotoxicology of Graphene-Family Nanomaterials: Standardised Descriptors, Explainable Machine Learning and Safe-by-Design
papers.abstract: Graphene-family nanomaterials (GFNs) comprise structurally and chemically diverse two-dimensional materials with broad applications in biomedicine, environmental technologies, energy, sensing, and advanced materials. Their expanding use has increased the need for reliable approaches to characterize and predict potential biological and environmental hazards. However, meaningful comparison of GFN toxicity data remains difficult because biological responses depend on interacting material characteristics, including lateral dimensions, layer number, defects, oxidation, surface functionalization, charge, morphology, aggregation, and dispersion state, together with exposure conditions, dosimetry, biological models, and endpoint definitions. This review examines how standardized descriptors can provide a quantitative basis for connecting GFN characteristics with toxicological responses and constructing reproducible predictive datasets. Structural, chemical, surface, colloidal, electronic, computational, exposure and biological descriptors are considered within an integrated framework that distinguishes intrinsic material properties from exposure-state characteristics. Particular emphasis is placed on descriptor harmonization, dataset curation, data provenance, and consistent reporting of measurement and dose information. The review also discusses machine-learning approaches for modelling nonlinear and multidimensional relationships between GFN descriptors and toxicity, emphasising the significance of proper feature selection, validation, applicability-domain assessment and uncertainty quantification. Because GFN datasets may contain limited numbers of independently characterized materials and substantial variation in experimental protocols, predictive performance should be interpreted in the context of data quality, validation design, and applicability-domain limitations. Explainable machine learning is considered as a means of identifying influential descriptors and generating mechanistically testable hypotheses rather than causal conclusions. Building on these principles, a standardized predictive framework is proposed that links characterization, descriptor harmonization, toxicity datasets, validated and explainable machine learning, experimental confirmation, and iterative model refinement. The framework provides a foundation for using predictive insights to guide material modification and support Safe-by-Design and Safe-and-Sustainable-by-Design strategies. Overall, standardized descriptors and traceable data practices can help advance GFN nanotoxicology from heterogeneous retrospective comparisons toward reproducible, interpretable, and experimentally testable prediction.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks for three-dimensional droplet dynamics in two-phase pressure-driven channel flow
papers.abstract: The accurate computational modeling of two-phase flows, particularly the tracking of moving interfaces and complex fluid dynamics, remains a significant challenge in applied mechanics. In this work, we present a computational framework that uses physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to solve the governing multiphase Navier Stokes equations, along with the volume of fluid (VOF) method to capture interface dynamics. To assess the robustness and accuracy of the proposed methodology, we simulate the transient dynamics and deformation of a droplet in a fully developed microchannel flow. The performance of the PINN framework is systematically evaluated across varying capillary numbers, droplet radii, and viscosity ratios. By embedding the physical conservation laws and the VOF advection equation directly into the neural network's loss functions, the PINN approach successfully resolves the complex interplay of inertial, viscous, and interfacial forces. Validation demonstrates that the proposed computational framework accurately captures droplet deformation, achieving maximum droplet deformation errors of less than 8%. These findings establish the proposed PINN-based framework as a physically consistent, data-free in training, and accurate alternative to conventional numerical solvers, advancing the mathematical modeling of complex multiphase systems.

papers.title: Health-Constrained Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Subject-Specific Chemotherapy Dosing Under Parameter Variability and Model Mismatch: A Simulation-Based Proof of Concept
papers.abstract: Selecting an appropriate chemotherapy dose is challenging because tumor growth is nonlinear, treatment can affect physiological condition, and tumor–drug responses vary across subjects. This study extends the third-order tumor–drug model of Siket et al. with a normalized, phenomenological physiological-health state and formulates a health-constrained nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) framework that combines tumor suppression, health preservation, and control smoothness under the simulation-defined constraint xh≥80. Simulations were conducted on eight virtual Siket parameter profiles. At λ=0.50, PLD3, PLD4, and PLD6 achieved tumor-volume reductions of approximately 74.7%, 73.4%, and 77.6%, respectively, whereas the other five profiles showed tumor progression. The structural indicator ρ=a−b−n was strongly negatively associated with tumor reduction (Pearson correlation of approximately −0.91 for all profiles and −0.98 excluding PLD1); this is a descriptive observation based on only eight profiles. A dose-matched comparison with a simple threshold-based strategy favored NMPC for some profiles, although the health constraint was not imposed on the comparator. The health bound was satisfied in all 15 one-at-a-time mismatch cases, but joint parameter perturbations produced threshold violations and optimization difficulties for PLD1 and PLD9, and health-model sensitivity analyses revealed further difficulties for PLD1. The health model and its threshold are not calibrated against clinical data. This work is a simulation-based proof of concept and does not establish clinical safety, clinical efficacy, or general robustness.

papers.title: Model predictive control of polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells considering spatially distributed operational constraints
papers.abstract: Dynamic operation is a major driver of locally occurring degradation in polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells, thus limiting their lifetime. This work presents a predictive control scheme for tracking highly dynamic power demand while limiting exposure to local safety-critical conditions, such as reactant starvation. The underlying prediction model combines reduced-order local linear models derived from a distributed-parameter fuel cell model to efficiently represent nonlinear cell dynamics. An extended Kalman filter estimates internal state distributions and provides reduced-order state feedback to the controller. A simulation scenario based on a WLTP cycle assesses the control scheme under realistic dynamic operating conditions. The average computation time per control step is below the sampling interval, supporting the feasibility of real-time implementation. Compared with PID and MPC baselines, the proposed scheme achieves comparable power-tracking accuracy while improving overall compliance with spatially distributed safety constraints, thereby reducing exposure to degradation-promoting operating conditions.

papers.title: Nursing Students' Knowledge of and Attitudes to Pressure Injury Prevention: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The aim of this study was to examine existing evidence about undergraduate nursing students' knowledge of and attitudes towards pressure injury prevention. A systematic review of primary qualitative, quantitative, and mixed‐methods studies was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A convergent mixed‐methods synthesis was undertaken. Methodological quality was appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). MEDLINE, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science, and ERIC were searched on 21 August 2025 for literature published between January 2010 and 21 August 2025. Fifty‐eight studies from 26 countries met the inclusion criteria. Nursing students demonstrated suboptimal knowledge of pressure injury prevention, with mean scores on validated tools (PUKAT/PUKAT 2.0) ranging from 23.5% to 61%, and a pooled mean of 39.2%. Attitudes towards pressure injury prevention were generally positive, with most studies reporting scores > 75% on the APUP instrument and similar tools. Qualitative findings highlighted gaps between theoretical instruction and clinical practice and a need for experiential and simulation‐based learning. Despite positive attitudes, nursing students' knowledge of pressure injury prevention remains inadequate globally. Curriculum redesign incorporating active learning strategies, simulation, and integration of theory with practice is essential.

papers.abstract: This research aimed to 1) study the role of school administrators in developing instructional media to promote active learning in Buddhism, 2) develop instructional media through digital platforms to promote active learning in Buddhism in Moral Teaching Monk Schools in Roi Et Province, and 3) evaluate the impact of using instructional media through digital platforms to promote active learning in Buddhism in Moral Teaching Monk Schools in Roi Et Province. The study employed a mixed-methods design. The conceptual framework drew on Benyapha Phatthanaphiphat and Natchaphak Mi-usa’s concept of platform-based instructional media development and Kittichai Suthasinobon’s concept of Buddhist teaching skills. The population consisted of 430 school administrators and moral teaching monks in Moral Teaching Monk Schools in Roi Et Province. The sample size, calculated using Taro Yamane’s formula, was 235. The research instrument was a five-point rating scale questionnaire. Data were analyzed using frequency, percentage, mean, standard deviation, and Pearson’s correlation coefficient. For the qualitative phase, in-depth interviews were conducted with 13 key informants, who were school directors under the Roi Et Primary Educational Service Area Office 1, and a focus group discussion was held with six experts. The results revealed the following: 1) The role of school administrators in developing instructional media to promote active learning in Buddhism was, overall, at a high level. The roles in instructional media design and development, the use of technology and online platforms, and the appropriateness of media content and format were significantly correlated with the development of Buddhist teaching skills at the .01 level. 2) The design and development of instructional media can enhance students’ learning by fostering skills, understanding, and morality and ethics in daily life, which will contribute to developing citizens of quality in both secular and spiritual dimensions in the future. 3) The impact of using the instructional media was that their design and development increased learning efficiency and promoted the creation of diverse media.

papers.abstract: This research aimed to (1) study the body of knowledge on developing social studies teachers’ competencies based on Buddhist teaching methods, (2) assess the needs for developing an instructional system, (3) develop an instructional system based on the concept of active learning in accordance with Buddhist teaching methods, and (4) test and evaluate the quality of the developed instructional system under the Secondary Educational Service Area Office Uthai Thani Chainat. This research and development study employed a mixed-methods approach. The sample consisted of 108 social studies teachers, and the 10 key informants, comprising monks and laypersons, were selected through purposive sampling. The research instruments included a questionnaire, an interview form, an instructional system evaluation form, an achievement test, and a satisfaction questionnaire. Data were analyzed using percentage, mean, standard deviation, t-test, effectiveness index (E.I.), and content analysis. The results revealed the following: (1) The body of knowledge comprised five core competencies, six functional competencies, active learning, and four principles of Buddhist teaching methods, integrated with the CIPOF Model. (2) Teachers needed an instructional system that emphasized learner participation. All teachers (100.00%) reported problems with the suitability of content relative to instructional time and expressed a need for instructional innovation, 80.00% reported problems with learning achievement, and 70.00% considered instructional media insufficient. (3) The developed instructional system consisted of eight components: context analysis, inputs, preparation, learning activities, assessment, conclusion, outputs, and system improvement, with a five-step instructional process. The evaluation of the draft prototype by five experts found that both the main components of the instructional system and the process component were appropriate at a high level. (4) The tryouts of the instructional system yielded effectiveness indices of 0.66, 0.68, and 0.71 in the preliminary tests, respectively, and 0.72 in the field implementation. Students’ posttest achievement was significantly higher than their pretest achievement (t = 34.427, p < .001). Students’ satisfaction was at a high level, and the qualified experts’ certification of the instructional system was also at a high level.
